title.raw: 卷25 志第20 刑法 Volume 25 Treatises 20: Punishment and Law

sentences.zh: 夫刑者，制死生之命，詳善惡之源，翦亂誅暴，禁人為非者也。

translations.literal: As for punishment, it regulates the mandate of life and death, examines the source of good and evil, cuts off disorder and punishes the violent, and restrains people from doing wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment is what controls life and death, traces good and evil to their roots, suppresses rebellion and executes the violent, and keeps people from wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 聖王仰視法星，旁觀習坎，彌縫五氣，取則四時，莫不先春風以播恩，後秋霜而動憲。

translations.literal: The sage kings looked up at the constellation of law, observed Kan on the side, harmonized the five qi, and took their model from the four seasons—none failed first to spread favor like the spring wind, then to deploy authority like the autumn frost.
translations.idiomatic: Sage kings looked to the stars of law and the trigram of peril, harmonizing the five elemental forces and taking the four seasons as their model: always spreading grace like the spring wind before enforcing law like the autumn frost.

sentences.zh: 是以宣慈惠愛，導其萌芽，刑罰威怒，隨其肅殺。

translations.literal: Therefore they proclaimed kindness and benevolence to guide things at the budding stage, and wielded the authority and wrath of punishment in accord with the stern killing of autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Thus they nurtured mercy and affection while wrongdoing was still in bud, and deployed the stern authority of punishment when severity was required.

sentences.zh: 仁恩以為情性，禮義以為綱紀，養化以為本，明刑以為助。

translations.literal: They took benevolence and grace as emotional nature, ritual and righteousness as the guiding threads, nurturing and transformation as the foundation, and enlightened punishment as the auxiliary.
translations.idiomatic: Benevolence was their disposition, ritual the framework, moral cultivation the foundation, and clear law the supporting force.

sentences.zh: 上有道，刑之而無刑；

translations.literal: When the ruler above has the Way, he applies punishment yet there is effectively no punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Under a ruler who holds the Way, punishment is applied yet crime scarcely exists.

sentences.zh: 上無道，殺之而不勝也。

translations.literal: When the ruler above lacks the Way, he kills yet cannot prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Under a ruler without the Way, even execution cannot stem the tide of crime.

sentences.zh: 記曰：「教之以德，齊之以禮，則人有格心。

translations.literal: The Record says: "If you instruct them with virtue and harmonize them with ritual, then people will have a mind of reverence and self-correction."
translations.idiomatic: The Record says: "Teach people through virtue and align them through ritual, and they will develop a reverent heart."

sentences.zh: 教之以政，齊之以刑，則人有遁心。

translations.literal: "If you instruct them with governance and harmonize them with punishment, then people will have a mind of evasion."
translations.idiomatic: "Instruct them through statute and regulate them through punishment, and they will harbor only thoughts of evasion."

sentences.zh: 」而始乎勸善，終乎禁暴，以此字人，必兼刑罰。

translations.literal: Beginning with exhorting the good and ending with restraining violence, to govern people in this way, one must combine both punishment and penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Beginning with encouragement of virtue and ending with suppression of violence—governing people in this manner requires punishment as well.

sentences.zh: 至於時逢交泰，政稱忠厚，美化與車軌攸同，至仁與嘉祥間出，歲布平典，年垂簡憲。

translations.literal: As for when the times encounter mutual peace and flourishing, government is called generous and sincere, transforming influence extends as far as cart tracks, supreme benevolence and auspicious omens appear in succession, each year promulgates equitable statutes, each year hangs forth concise laws.
translations.idiomatic: In ages of perfect harmony, when government is praised for its sincerity, moral influence reaches everywhere carts may travel, supreme benevolence and good omens appear in turn, and equitable statutes are issued year after year.

sentences.zh: 昭然如日月，望之者不迷，曠乎如大路，行之者不惑。

translations.literal: Clear as the sun and moon—those who look upon them are not lost; vast as the great road—those who travel it are not confused.
translations.idiomatic: Clear as sun and moon, so that none who look upon them lose their way; broad as a great highway, so that none who walk it go astray.

sentences.zh: 刑者甲兵焉，鈇鉞焉，刀鋸鑽鑿，鞭扑榎楚，陳乎原野而肆諸市朝，其所由來，亦已久矣。

translations.literal: Punishment comprises armor and weapons, axes and great axes, knives, saws, drills, and awls, whips, beatings, and the mulberry and thorn rods—displayed in open country and exposed in market and court. Its origin, too, is of long standing.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment takes the form of armor and weapons, axes and halberds, knives, saws, drills, and awls, whips and cudgels, mulberry rods and thorn switches—displayed in the open fields and exposed in market and court. Its origins, too, stretch far back in time.

sentences.zh: 若夫龍官之歲，鳳紀之前，結繩而不違，不令而人畏。

translations.literal: As for the age of the Dragon officials, before the era of the Phoenix chronicle, people tied knots and did not transgress, and without commands people feared.
translations.idiomatic: In the age of the Dragon officials, before the Phoenix chronicle, people used knotted cords and did not transgress; without being commanded, they lived in awe.

sentences.zh: 五帝畫象，殊其衣服，三王肉刑，刻其膚體。

translations.literal: The Five Emperors painted images, distinguishing their clothing; the Three Kings used corporal punishment, carving their flesh and bodies.
translations.idiomatic: The Five Emperors marked punishments on painted images and distinguished offenses by dress; the Three Dynasties applied corporal punishment, marking the flesh and body.

sentences.zh: 若重華之眚災肆赦，文命之刑罰三千，而都君卹刑，尚奉唐堯之德，高密泣罪，猶懷虞舜之心。

translations.literal: When Chonghua suffered calamity and granted general amnesty, when Wenming's punishments numbered three thousand, yet the Lord of Yong sympathized with punishment and still upheld the virtue of Tang Yao, Gao Mi wept over guilt and still harbored the heart of Yu Shun.
translations.idiomatic: Even when Emperor Shun, stricken by calamity, granted universal amnesty, and when Yu's code listed three thousand punishments—the Lord of Yong still mourned the use of punishment and upheld the virtue of Emperor Yao, and Gao Yao wept over guilt and still cherished the heart of Emperor Shun.

sentences.zh: 殷因以降，去德滋遠。

translations.literal: From the Yin dynasty downward, they departed further and further from virtue.
translations.idiomatic: From the Shang dynasty onward, rulers drifted ever further from virtue.

sentences.zh: 若紂能遵成湯，不造炮格，設刑兼禮，守位依仁，則西伯斂轡，化為田叟。

translations.literal: If Zhou had been able to follow Cheng Tang, not constructing the roasting pillar, setting up punishments combined with ritual, maintaining the throne in accord with benevolence, then the Lord of the West would have reined in his horses and been transformed into an old farmer in the fields.
translations.idiomatic: Had King Zhou followed the ways of King Tang, forsworn the roasting pillar, blended punishment with ritual, and held the throne through benevolence, the Lord of the West would have reined in his horses and become an ordinary farmer.

sentences.zh: 周王立三刺以不濫，弘三宥以開物，成、康以四十二年之間，刑厝不用。

translations.literal: King Wu of Zhou established the three interrogations so as not to be excessive, enlarged the three pardons to open things up; during the forty-two years of Cheng and Kang, punishments were set aside and not used.
translations.idiomatic: King Wu of Zhou instituted three rounds of interrogation to prevent excess, and expanded the three grounds for pardon to show compassion; during the forty-two years of Kings Cheng and Kang, punishment was laid aside altogether.

sentences.zh: 薰風潛暢，頌聲遐舉，越裳重譯，萬里來歸。

translations.literal: The fragrant breeze flowed secretly and smoothly, eulogistic songs rose from afar, the people of Yue bearing interpreters came from ten thousand li to submit.
translations.idiomatic: A gentle breeze permeated the realm, songs of praise rose from afar, and the people of Yue, bearing interpreters, came from ten thousand li to pay tribute.

sentences.zh: 若乃魯接燕、齊，荊鄰鄭、晉，時之所尚，資乎辯舌，國之所恃，不在威刑。

translations.literal: As for Lu bordering Yan and Qi, and Chu neighboring Zheng and Jin—what the times valued lay in eloquent tongues; what the states relied upon was not awesome punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu bordered Yan and Qi, and Chu neighbored Zheng and Jin, the age prized skill in debate, and states relied not on harsh punishment but on persuasion.

sentences.zh: 是以纔鼓夷蒐，宣尼致誚，既鑄刑辟，叔向貽書。

translations.literal: Therefore when the Jin drum and Yi hunt took place, Confucius expressed censure; once the penal inscriptions were cast, Shu Xiang sent his letter of remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin held the autumn hunt at Yi, Confucius expressed his disapproval; when penal inscriptions were cast in bronze, Shu Xiang sent his letter of protest.

sentences.zh: 夫勃澥之浸，沾濡千里，列國之政，豈周之膏潤者歟！

translations.literal: The rush of the boiling sea, soaking and moistening for a thousand li—the governance of the feudal states, was it not nourished by the enriching moisture of Zhou!
translations.idiomatic: Like boiling seawater spreading its moisture for a thousand li—the politics of the feudal states were surely nurtured by the enriching influence of Zhou!

sentences.zh: 秦氏僻自西戎，初平區夏，于時投戈棄甲，仰恩祈惠，乃落嚴霜於政教，揮流電於邦國，棄灰偶語，生愁怨於前，毒網凝科，害肌膚於後。

translations.literal: The Qin clan, secluded in the western Rong, when first pacifying the central realm, at that time cast aside weapons and armor, looking upward for grace and praying for favor—yet they let severe frost fall upon government and teaching, swung lightning across the realm, discarded ash and casual speech bringing resentment in advance, and the net of poison and frozen statutes harmed flesh and skin afterward.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin, isolated in the western frontier, when first pacifying the central realm cast aside arms and looked to their conquerors for mercy—yet they brought harsh frost upon government and teaching, struck their domain with lightning, and with prohibitions on discarded ashes and casual conversation bred resentment at every turn, while their cruel statutes damaged body and soul.

sentences.zh: 玄鉞肆於朝市，赭服飄於路衢，將閭有一劍之哀，茅焦請列星之數。

translations.literal: The dark battle-axe was wielded in market and court, red-clad convicts drifted along the roads; Jiang Lu had the grief of a single sword, Mao Jiao requested the number of the stars.
translations.idiomatic: Dark axes were swung in market and court, red-clad convicts wandered the highways; Jiang Lu mourned with the grief of a single sword, and Mao Jiao petitioned for the tally of the stars.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖初以三章之約，以慰秦人，孝文躬親玄默，遂疎天網。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu of Han initially used the covenant of three articles to comfort the people of Qin; Emperor Xiaowen personally practiced deep silence and thus loosened Heaven's net.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu of Han at first offered the three-article covenant to reassure the people of Qin; Emperor Wen personally cultivated silent humility and thereby loosened the net of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 孝宣樞機周密，法理詳備，選于定國為廷尉，黃霸以為廷平。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaoxuan was meticulous and thorough in the pivots of power, detailed and complete in legal principles; he selected Yu Dingguo as Commandant of Justice and made Huang Ba the Tribunal Assessor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan was meticulous in the machinery of state and thorough in legal doctrine; he appointed Yu Dingguo Commandant of Justice and Huang Ba Tribunal Assessor.

sentences.zh: 每以季秋之後，諸所請讞，帝常幸宣室，齋而決事，明察平恕，號為寬簡。

translations.literal: After each autumn season, for all cases submitted for review, the emperor often visited the Hall of Illumination, fasted, and decided matters—clear-sighted, fair, and forgiving, called lenient and simple.
translations.idiomatic: Each year after the autumn equinox, when cases came up for review, the emperor would visit the Hall of Illumination, fast, and pass judgment—keen-eyed, fair, and clement, earning a reputation for lenity and simplicity.

sentences.zh: 光武中興，不移其舊，是以二漢羣后，罕聞殘酷。

translations.literal: When Emperor Guangwu restored the dynasty, he did not alter these precedents; thus among the sovereigns of the two Han dynasties, cruel punishments were rarely heard of.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Guangwu restored the Han, he kept these practices unchanged; thus among the rulers of the two Han dynasties, cruel punishment was seldom heard of.

sentences.zh: 魏武造易釱之科，明皇施減死之令，中原凋敝，吳、蜀三分，哀矜折獄，亦所未暇。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Wei created the statute of easy shackles, Emperor Ming issued the order to reduce death sentences—the central plains were desolate and exhausted, Wu and Shu divided into three parts, and pity and restraint in judging cases was also what they had no leisure for.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Cao of Wei instituted lighter shackles, and Emperor Ming reduced death sentences—but the central plain lay in ruins, the realm was divided among three powers, and there was little time for compassionate restraint in judging cases.

sentences.zh: 晉氏平吳，九州寧一，乃命賈充，大明刑憲。

translations.literal: When the Jin dynasty pacified Wu, the Nine Provinces were united in peace, and they then ordered Jia Chong to greatly illuminate the penal statutes.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin pacified Wu and the Nine Provinces were united under one rule, Jia Chong was charged with codifying the penal law in full.

sentences.zh: 內以平章百姓，外以和協萬邦，實曰輕平，稱為簡易。

translations.literal: Internally to regulate and harmonize the common people, externally to harmonize the myriad states—it was truly called light and equitable, and known as simple and easy.
translations.idiomatic: It was meant to govern the people within and harmonize the myriad states without—and was praised as lenient, fair, and straightforward.

sentences.zh: 是以宋、齊方駕，轥其餘軌。

translations.literal: Thus Song and Qi drove abreast, crushing their remaining tracks.
translations.idiomatic: Song and Qi followed in their tracks, leaving little of their own mark behind.

sentences.zh: 若乃刑隨喜怒，道暌正直，布憲擬於秋荼，設網踰於朝脛，恣興夷翦，取快情靈。

translations.literal: As for when punishment followed likes and dislikes, the Way diverged from uprightness, statutes were spread like the autumn bitter-tea plant, nets were set beyond the morning shin, at will mass exterminations were raised, taking satisfaction from the emotions and spirit.
translations.idiomatic: When punishment followed whim, when justice was abandoned, when laws proliferated like autumn grass and traps were set beyond measure, when rulers slaughtered at will to satisfy their passions—

sentences.zh: 若隋高祖之揮刃無辜，齊文宣之輕刀臠割，此所謂匹夫私讎，非關國典。

translations.literal: Such as Emperor Gaozu of Sui wielding his blade against the innocent, and Emperor Wenxuan of Qi lightly wielding his knife in dismemberment—these are what are called the private vengeance of common men, not matters of national statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Such as Emperor Wen of Sui slaying the innocent at will, or Emperor Wenxuan of Northern Qi carving up victims with casual cruelty—these were the private vendettas of individual men, not the business of national law.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：「刑亂及諸政，政亂及諸身。

translations.literal: Confucius said: "When punishment is disordered it reaches to all government; when government is disordered it reaches to one's own person."
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: "When punishment falls into disorder, government follows; when government falls into disorder, the ruler himself suffers."

sentences.zh: 」心之所詣，則善惡之本原也。

translations.literal: What the heart aims at is the root source of good and evil.
translations.idiomatic: What the heart pursues is the root of good and evil.

sentences.zh: 彪、約所製，無刑法篇，臧、蕭之書，又多漏略。

translations.literal: What Biao and Yue produced had no chapter on penal law; the books of Zang and Xiao were furthermore many in omissions and lacunae.
translations.idiomatic: The histories compiled by Ban Biao and Ban Gu contained no chapter on penal law, and the works of Zang Rongxian and Xiao Fang lacked much besides.

sentences.zh: 是以撮其遺事，以至隋氏，附于篇云。

translations.literal: Therefore I gather their surviving records, down to the Sui dynasty, and attach them to this chapter.
translations.idiomatic: I therefore gather such surviving records down to the Sui dynasty and attach them to this chapter.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝承齊昏虐之餘，刑政多僻。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Liang, inheriting the remnants of Qi under its benighted and cruel rule, had many perverse practices in punishment and government.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang inherited the aftermath of Northern Qi's benighted and cruel rule, under which penal administration had grown deeply perverse.

sentences.zh: 既即位，乃制權典，依周、漢舊事，有罪者贖。

translations.literal: Once he ascended the throne, he then instituted provisional statutes, following the old precedents of Zhou and Han—those guilty could ransom themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Upon taking the throne, he instituted provisional statutes based on Zhou and Han precedent, under which offenders could redeem their penalties.

sentences.zh: 其科，凡在官身犯，罰金。

translations.literal: As for the statute categories: for all who while in office committed offenses personally, there was monetary fine.
translations.idiomatic: Under these statutes, all officials who committed offenses while in office were subject to monetary fines.

sentences.zh: 鞭杖杖督之罪，悉入贖停罰。

translations.literal: Crimes punishable by whip, cudgel, or beating for supervision were all absorbed into ransom and suspension of penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Offenses normally punished by whipping, beating, or supervised flogging could all be redeemed and the physical penalty waived.

sentences.zh: 其臺省令史士卒欲贖者，聽之。

translations.literal: Those among secretariat clerks, provincial staff, soldiers, and conscripts who wished to redeem were permitted to do so.
translations.idiomatic: Secretarial clerks, provincial staff, soldiers, and conscripts who wished to redeem their penalties were permitted to do so.

sentences.zh: 時欲議定律令，得齊時舊郎濟陽蔡法度，家傳律學，云齊武時，刪定郎王植之，集注張、杜舊律，合為一書，凡一千五百三十條，事未施行，其文殆滅。

translations.literal: At the time they wished to deliberate on fixing statutes and ordinances, and found Cai Fadu of Jiyang, an old clerk from Qi times, whose family transmitted the learning of law. He said: in Wu of Qi's time, the revising clerk Wang Zhizhi collected and annotated the old statutes of Zhang and Du, combining them into one book of 1,530 articles in total—the matter was not implemented, and the text was nearly lost.
translations.idiomatic: When they sought to revise the code, they found Cai Fadu of Jiyang, a former Qi clerk whose family had preserved the legal tradition. He reported that under Emperor Wu of Qi, the revising clerk Wang Zhizhi had compiled and annotated the Zhang and Du commentaries on the old code into a single work of 1,530 articles—the project had never been enacted, and the text was nearly lost.

sentences.zh: 法度能言之。

translations.literal: Fadu was able to speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: Fadu was able to recite it from memory.

sentences.zh: 於是以為兼尚書刪定郎，使損益植之舊本，以為梁律。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was appointed concurrent Revising Clerk in the Ministry of Justice, and charged to add to and reduce Wang Zhizhi's old text to serve as the Liang code.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed revising clerk in the Ministry of Justice and charged with revising Wang Zhizhi's original text to produce the Liang code.

sentences.zh: 天監元年八月，乃下詔曰：「律令不一，實難去弊。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Tianjian, an edict was issued saying: "Statutes and ordinances are not unified, and in truth it is hard to remove abuses."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Tianjian 1, an edict declared: "Where statutes and ordinances lack unity, abuses cannot easily be removed."

sentences.zh: [1]殺傷有法，昏墨有刑，此蓋常科，易為條例。

translations.literal: [1] There are laws for killing and wounding, punishments for obscurity and tattooing—These are standing categories, easily made into articles.
translations.idiomatic: "Laws for homicide and assault, penalties for obscuring truth and marking the face—these standing categories can readily be set down as articles."

sentences.zh: 至如三男一妻，懸首造獄，事非慮內，法出恒鈞。

translations.literal: As for three sons and one wife, hanging the head and building a prison—matters not within expected deliberation, law going beyond the constant balance.
translations.idiomatic: "But matters such as polygamy, capital display of severed heads, and arbitrary imprisonment—issues never intended for routine deliberation, yet laws that fall outside the ordinary measure—"

sentences.zh: 前王之律，後王之令，因循創附，良各有以。

translations.literal: The statutes of former kings, the edicts of later kings—following precedent and adding new provisions, each indeed had its reason.
translations.idiomatic: "Former kings' statutes and later kings' edicts accumulated by precedent, each with its own rationale—"

sentences.zh: 若遊辭費句，無取於實錄者，宜悉除之。

translations.literal: If there are circuitous phrases wasting clauses with no use for factual record, they should all be removed.
translations.idiomatic: "—but flowery language and redundant clauses that serve no practical purpose should all be removed."

sentences.zh: 求文指歸，可適變者，載一家為本，用眾家以附。

translations.literal: Seek the intent of the text; what can suit change—take one school as the base and use the many schools as appendices.
translations.idiomatic: "Seek the essential meaning of the text; where adaptation is needed, take one commentary as the base and attach the others as supplements."

sentences.zh: 丙丁俱有，則去丁以存丙。

translations.literal: If both Bing and Ding have provisions, remove Ding and keep Bing.
translations.idiomatic: "If provisions by Bing and Ding overlap, retain Bing and discard Ding."

sentences.zh: 若丙丁二事，注釋不同，則二家兼載。

translations.literal: If on a matter both Bing and Ding have different annotations, then carry both schools.
translations.idiomatic: "If Bing and Ding offer different interpretations of the same matter, include both."

sentences.zh: 咸使百司，議其可不，取其可安，以為標例。

translations.literal: Have all the hundred offices jointly deliberate what is feasible and infeasible, take what can be settled, and use it as the standard example.
translations.idiomatic: "Let all offices debate what is and is not workable, adopt what can be reliably applied, and establish it as the standard precedent."

sentences.zh: 宜云『某等如干人同議，以此為長』，則定以為梁律。

translations.literal: It should read 'So-and-so and such-and-such number of people jointly deliberated, taking this as superior'—then fix it as the Liang code.
translations.idiomatic: "Record that 'So-and-so and X others jointly deliberated and adopted this as the superior reading'—and then fix the result as the Liang code."

sentences.zh: 留尚書比部，悉使備文，若班下州郡，止撮機要。

translations.literal: Retain it in the Comparison Section of the Ministry of Justice with the full text complete; if distributed to prefectures and commanderies, only extract the essentials.
translations.idiomatic: "Keep the complete text on file in the Ministry of Justice's Comparison Section; when issuing copies to prefectures and commanderies, send only the essentials."

sentences.zh: 可無二門侮法之弊。

translations.literal: Thus there can be no harm of two gates insulting the law.
translations.idiomatic: "This will prevent the abuse of conflicting legal gates."

sentences.zh: 」法度又請曰：「魏、晉撰律，止關數人，今若皆諮列位，恐緩而無決。」

translations.literal: Fadu further petitioned saying: "When Wei and Jin compiled statutes, they concerned only a few persons; if now all offices are consulted, I fear it will be slow and without decision."
translations.idiomatic: Fadu further petitioned: "When Wei and Jin drafted their codes, only a handful of people were involved; if we now consult every office, I fear deliberation will drag on without resolution."

sentences.zh: 於是以尚書令王亮、侍中王瑩、尚書僕射沈約、吏部尚書范雲、長兼侍中柳惲、給事黃門侍郎傅昭、通直散騎常侍孔藹、御史中丞樂藹、太常丞許懋等，參議斷定，定為二十篇：一曰刑名，二曰法例，三曰盜劫，四曰賊叛，五曰詐偽，六曰受賕，七曰告劾，八曰討捕，九曰繫訊，十曰斷獄，十一曰雜，十二曰戶，十三曰擅興，十四曰毀亡，十五曰衞宮，十六曰水火，十七曰倉庫，十八曰廐，十九曰關市，二十曰違制。

translations.literal: Thereupon Wang Liang, Minister of Justice, Wang Ying, Palace Attendant, Shen Yue, Vice Minister of Justice, Fan Yun, Minister of Personnel, Liu Yun concurrently Palace Attendant, Fu Zhao, Supervising Secretary of the Yellow Gate, Kong Ai, Regular Attendant on Direct Communication, Yue Ai, Imperial Censor, Xu Mao, Vice Director of the Court of Sacrifices, and others jointly deliberated and fixed it, determining twenty chapters: first, Names of Punishments; second, Legal Precedents; third, Robbery and Plunder; fourth, Rebellion and Treason; fifth, Fraud and Forgery; sixth, Accepting Bribes; seventh, Accusation and Impeachment; eighth, Pursuit and Capture; ninth, Detention and Interrogation; tenth, Trial and Judgment; eleventh, Miscellaneous; twelfth, Household Registers; thirteenth, Unauthorized Mobilization; fourteenth, Destruction and Loss; fifteenth, Palace Guard; sixteenth, Fire and Water; seventeenth, Granaries and Storehouses; eighteenth, Stables; nineteenth, Passes and Markets; twentieth, Violating Regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Liang, Wang Ying, Shen Yue, Fan Yun, Liu Yun, Fu Zhao, Kong Ai, Yue Ai, Xu Mao, and others were appointed to finalize the code in twenty chapters: Names of Punishments, Legal Precedents, Robbery and Plunder, Rebellion and Treason, Fraud and Forgery, Accepting Bribes, Accusation and Impeachment, Pursuit and Capture, Detention and Interrogation, Trial and Judgment, Miscellaneous, Household Registers, Unauthorized Mobilization, Destruction and Loss, Palace Guard, Fire and Water, Granaries and Storehouses, Stables, Passes and Markets, and Violating Regulations.

sentences.zh: 其制刑為十五等之差：棄市已上為死罪，大罪梟其首，其次棄市。

translations.literal: They fixed punishments as fifteen degrees of difference: above public execution was death penalty; for great crimes the head was exposed, for lesser ones public execution.
translations.idiomatic: Capital punishment was divided into two degrees: for major crimes the head was displayed, for lesser ones the convict was executed in the market.

sentences.zh: 刑二歲已上為耐罪，言各隨伎能而任使之也。

translations.literal: Punishment of two years and above was nai offense—meaning each according to skill and ability was assigned duties.
translations.idiomatic: Terms of two years or more constituted "service penalties," meaning convicts were assigned labor according to their skills.

sentences.zh: 有髠鉗五歲刑，笞二百，收贖絹，男子六十疋。

translations.literal: There was the punishment of shaved head and cangue for five years, one hundred strokes of the rod, and ransom in silk—sixty bolts for a man.
translations.idiomatic: Shaved head and cangue for five years, plus two hundred strokes of the rod, could be redeemed with sixty bolts of silk for a man.

sentences.zh: 又有四歲刑，男子四十八疋。

translations.literal: There was also the four-year punishment—forty-eight bolts for a man.
translations.idiomatic: A four-year term could be redeemed with forty-eight bolts for a man.

sentences.zh: 又有三歲刑，男子三十六疋。

translations.literal: There was also the three-year punishment—thirty-six bolts for a man.
translations.idiomatic: A three-year term could be redeemed with thirty-six bolts for a man.

sentences.zh: 又有二歲刑，男子二十四疋。

translations.literal: There was also the two-year punishment—twenty-four bolts for a man.
translations.idiomatic: A two-year term could be redeemed with twenty-four bolts for a man.

sentences.zh: 罰金一兩已上為贖罪。

translations.literal: Monetary fine of one liang and above was ransom offense.
translations.idiomatic: Monetary fines of one liang or more constituted redeemable offenses.

sentences.zh: 贖死者金二斤，男子十六疋。

translations.literal: Ransom for death was two jin of gold—sixteen bolts for a man.
translations.idiomatic: Death could be redeemed with two jin of gold, or sixteen bolts of silk for a man.

sentences.zh: 贖髠鉗五歲刑笞二百者，金一斤十二兩，男子十四疋。

translations.literal: Ransom for shaved head and cangue five-year punishment with two hundred rod strokes was one jin twelve liang of gold—fourteen bolts for a man.
translations.idiomatic: Redemption of shaved head and cangue for five years plus two hundred rod strokes required one jin twelve liang of gold, or fourteen bolts for a man.

sentences.zh: 贖四歲刑者，金一斤八兩，男子十二疋。

translations.literal: Ransom for four-year punishment was one jin eight liang of gold—twelve bolts for a man.
translations.idiomatic: A four-year term required one jin eight liang of gold, or twelve bolts for a man.

sentences.zh: 贖三歲刑者，金一斤四兩，男子十疋。

translations.literal: Ransom for three-year punishment was one jin four liang of gold—ten bolts for a man.
translations.idiomatic: A three-year term required one jin four liang of gold, or ten bolts for a man.

sentences.zh: 贖二歲刑者，金一斤，男子八疋。

translations.literal: Ransom for two-year punishment was one jin of gold—eight bolts for a man.
translations.idiomatic: A two-year term required one jin of gold, or eight bolts for a man.

sentences.zh: 罰金十二兩者，男子六疋。

translations.literal: For monetary fine of twelve liang—six bolts for a man.
translations.idiomatic: A fine of twelve liang could be redeemed with six bolts for a man.

sentences.zh: 罰金八兩者，男子四疋。

translations.literal: For monetary fine of eight liang—four bolts for a man.
translations.idiomatic: A fine of eight liang could be redeemed with four bolts for a man.

sentences.zh: 罰金四兩者，男子二疋。

translations.literal: For monetary fine of four liang—two bolts for a man.
translations.idiomatic: A fine of four liang could be redeemed with two bolts for a man.

sentences.zh: 罰金二兩者，男子一疋。

translations.literal: For monetary fine of two liang—one bolt for a man.
translations.idiomatic: A fine of two liang could be redeemed with one bolt for a man.

sentences.zh: 罰金一兩者，男子二丈。

translations.literal: For monetary fine of one liang—two zhang for a man.
translations.idiomatic: A fine of one liang could be redeemed with two zhang of silk for a man.

sentences.zh: 女子各半之。

translations.literal: For women, each was half.
translations.idiomatic: Women paid half these amounts.

sentences.zh: 五刑不簡，正于五罰，五罰不服，正于五過，以贖論，故為此十五等之差。

translations.literal: When the five punishments are not sufficient, correct by the five fines; when the five fines are not accepted, correct by the five pardons—discussed according to ransom, hence these fifteen degrees of difference were made.
translations.idiomatic: When the five corporal punishments could not resolve a case, the five fines applied; when fines failed, the five pardons applied—with ransom as the governing principle, these fifteen degrees were established.

sentences.zh: 又制九等之差：有一歲刑，半歲刑，百日刑，鞭杖二百，鞭杖一百，鞭杖五十，鞭杖三十，鞭杖二十，鞭杖一十。

translations.literal: They also fixed nine degrees of difference: one-year punishment, half-year punishment, hundred-day punishment, two hundred strokes of whip, one hundred strokes of whip, fifty strokes of whip, thirty strokes of whip, twenty strokes of whip, ten strokes of whip.
translations.idiomatic: Nine lesser degrees were also established: one year, half year, hundred days, and whip penalties of two hundred, one hundred, fifty, thirty, twenty, and ten strokes.

sentences.zh: 又有八等之差：一曰免官，加杖督一百；

translations.literal: There were also eight degrees of difference: first, dismissal from office plus supervised beating of one hundred strokes;
translations.idiomatic: Eight administrative degrees were also established: first, dismissal from office plus one hundred strokes of supervised beating;

sentences.zh: 二曰免官；

translations.literal: second, dismissal from office;
translations.idiomatic: second, dismissal from office alone;

sentences.zh: 三曰奪勞百日，杖督一百；

translations.literal: third, deprivation of salary for one hundred days plus supervised beating of one hundred strokes;
translations.idiomatic: third, suspension of salary for one hundred days plus one hundred strokes of supervised beating;

sentences.zh: 四曰杖督一百；

translations.literal: fourth, supervised beating of one hundred strokes;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, one hundred strokes of supervised beating;

sentences.zh: 五曰杖督五十；

translations.literal: fifth, supervised beating of fifty strokes;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, fifty strokes of supervised beating;

sentences.zh: 六曰杖督三十；

translations.literal: sixth, supervised beating of thirty strokes;
translations.idiomatic: sixth, thirty strokes of supervised beating;

sentences.zh: 七曰杖督二十；

translations.literal: seventh, supervised beating of twenty strokes;
translations.idiomatic: seventh, twenty strokes of supervised beating;

sentences.zh: 八曰杖督一十。

translations.literal: eighth, supervised beating of ten strokes.
translations.idiomatic: eighth, ten strokes of supervised beating.

sentences.zh: 論加者上就次，當減者下就次。

translations.literal: When increasing punishment, go up to the next degree; when decreasing, go down to the next degree.
translations.idiomatic: When aggravating a sentence, apply the next higher degree; when mitigating, the next lower.

sentences.zh: 凡繫獄者，不即答款，應加測罰，不得以人士為隔。

translations.literal: For all held in prison, if they do not immediately confess, interrogation under torture should be added, and one may not use status as a person of rank as a barrier.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners who did not confess promptly were subject to interrogation under torture, regardless of social rank.

sentences.zh: 若人士犯罰，違扞不款，宜測罰者，先參議牒啟，然後科行。

translations.literal: If a person of rank commits an offense and resists confession, and torture should be applied, first submit a memorial for joint deliberation and then impose it.
translations.idiomatic: When a person of rank resisted confession and torture was warranted, a memorial had first to be submitted for deliberation before the penalty could be applied.

sentences.zh: 斷食三日，聽家人進粥二升。

translations.literal: After three days without food, family members are permitted to bring two sheng of gruel.
translations.idiomatic: After three days without food, family members were permitted to bring two sheng of gruel.

sentences.zh: 女及老小，一百五十刻乃與粥，滿千刻而止。

translations.literal: For women, the elderly, and the young, only after one hundred fifty ke do they receive gruel, stopping at one thousand ke.
translations.idiomatic: For women, the elderly, and children, gruel was given only after one hundred fifty ke of fasting, and no further after one thousand ke.

sentences.zh: 囚有械、杻、斗械及鉗，[2]並立輕重大小之差，而為定制。

translations.literal: Prisoners had shackles, cangues, combined shackles and cangues, and cangues—[2] light and heavy, large and small degrees were all established as fixed regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners wore shackles, cangues, combined restraints, and leg irons—[2] with fixed regulations distinguishing light from heavy and large from small.

sentences.zh: 其鞭，有制鞭、法鞭、常鞭，凡三等之差。

translations.literal: As for whips, there were ceremonial whip, legal whip, and ordinary whip—three degrees of difference in all.
translations.idiomatic: Three types of whip were prescribed: ceremonial, legal, and ordinary.

sentences.zh: 制鞭，生革廉成；

translations.literal: Ceremonial whip: raw hide with the grain side intact;
translations.idiomatic: The ceremonial whip was made of raw hide with the smooth side left intact;

sentences.zh: 法鞭，生革去廉；

translations.literal: legal whip: raw hide with the grain side removed;
translations.idiomatic: the legal whip of raw hide with the smooth side stripped away;

sentences.zh: 常鞭，熟靼不去廉。

translations.literal: ordinary whip: tanned hide with the grain side not removed.
translations.idiomatic: the ordinary whip of tanned hide with the smooth side left on.

sentences.zh: [3]皆作鶴頭紐，長一尺一寸。

translations.literal: [3] All were made with crane-head knots, one chi one cun long.
translations.idiomatic: [3] All were made with crane-head knots, one chi one cun in length.

sentences.zh: 梢長二尺七寸，廣三分，[4]靶長二尺五寸。

translations.literal: The tip was two chi seven cun long, three fen wide, [4] the handle two chi five cun long.
translations.idiomatic: The lash was two chi seven cun long and three fen wide; [4] the handle was two chi five cun long.

sentences.zh: 杖皆用生荊，長六尺。

translations.literal: All cudgels used raw thornwood, six chi long.
translations.idiomatic: All beating rods were made of raw thornwood, six chi in length.

sentences.zh: 有大杖、法杖、小杖三等之差。

translations.literal: There were three degrees of difference: great cudgel, legal cudgel, and small cudgel.
translations.idiomatic: Three grades were prescribed: the great cudgel, the legal cudgel, and the small cudgel.

sentences.zh: 大杖，大頭圍一寸三分，小頭圍八分半。

translations.literal: Great cudgel: the large end one cun three fen in circumference, the small end eight and a half fen.
translations.idiomatic: The great cudgel measured one cun three fen around the thick end and eight and a half fen around the thin end.

sentences.zh: 法杖，圍一寸三分，小頭五分。

translations.literal: Legal cudgel: one cun three fen in circumference, the small end five fen.
translations.idiomatic: The legal cudgel measured one cun three fen around the thick end and five fen around the thin end.

sentences.zh: 小杖，圍一寸一分，小頭極杪。

translations.literal: Small cudgel: one cun one fen in circumference, the small end extremely tapered.
translations.idiomatic: The small cudgel measured one cun one fen around the thick end, tapering to a very fine tip.

sentences.zh: 諸督罰，大罪無過五十、三十，小者二十。

translations.literal: For all supervised beatings, for great offenses no more than fifty or thirty strokes, for lesser ones twenty.
translations.idiomatic: Supervised beatings were capped at fifty or thirty strokes for major offenses and twenty for minor ones.

sentences.zh: 當笞二百以上者，笞半，餘半後決，中分鞭杖。

translations.literal: When the rod punishment should be two hundred strokes or more, half is applied first and the remainder decided later, splitting equally between whip and cudgel.
translations.idiomatic: When two hundred or more rod strokes were prescribed, half was applied first and the remainder later, divided equally between whip and cudgel.

sentences.zh: 老小於律令當得鞭杖罰者，皆半之。

translations.literal: The elderly and young who under statutes and ordinances should receive whip or cudgel punishment—all were halved.
translations.idiomatic: Elderly and juvenile offenders received half the prescribed whip or cudgel strokes.

sentences.zh: 其應得法鞭、杖者，以熟靼鞭、小杖。

translations.literal: Those who should receive the legal whip or cudgel used the tanned whip and small cudgel.
translations.idiomatic: Offenders subject to legal whip or cudgel penalties were punished with the tanned whip and small cudgel.

sentences.zh: 過五十者，稍行之。

translations.literal: When exceeding fifty strokes, they were applied in stages.
translations.idiomatic: When more than fifty strokes were required, they were administered in stages.

sentences.zh: 將吏已上及女人應有罰者，以罰金代之。

translations.literal: Generals, officials, and above, and women who should receive punishment, had monetary fines substituted.
translations.idiomatic: Generals, officials, and women subject to physical punishment paid monetary fines instead.

sentences.zh: 其以職員應罰，[5]及律令指名制罰者，不用此令。

translations.literal: Those punished according to office rank, [5] and those with specifically named punishments in statutes and ordinances, did not use this ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: Offenses punished according to official rank, [5] or by specifically named penalties in the code, were exempt from this rule.

sentences.zh: 其問事諸罰，皆用熟靼鞭、小杖。

translations.literal: For all interrogation punishments, the tanned whip and small cudgel were used.
translations.idiomatic: Interrogation under torture employed the tanned whip and small cudgel.

sentences.zh: 其制鞭制杖，法鞭法杖，自非特詔，皆不得用。

translations.literal: Ceremonial whip, ceremonial cudgel, legal whip, and legal cudgel—unless by special edict, none could be used.
translations.idiomatic: Ceremonial and legal whips and cudgels could not be used except by special imperial edict.

sentences.zh: 詔鞭杖在京師者，皆於雲龍門行。

translations.literal: When edicts ordered whipping or cudgeling in the capital, all were carried out at the Cloud Dragon Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Capital punishments of whipping or cudgeling ordered by edict were carried out at the Cloud Dragon Gate.

sentences.zh: 女子懷孕者，勿得決罰。

translations.literal: Pregnant women must not be sentenced and punished.
translations.idiomatic: Pregnant women were exempt from sentencing and punishment.

sentences.zh: 其謀反、降叛、大逆已上皆斬。

translations.literal: Rebellion, surrender and betrayal, and great treason and above—all were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Rebellion, defection, and great treason and above were all punished by beheading.

sentences.zh: 父子同產男，無少長，皆棄市。

translations.literal: Fathers and sons of the same household, males regardless of age—all were executed in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Fathers and sons of the same household, regardless of age, were all executed in the market.

sentences.zh: 母妻姊妹及應從坐棄市者，妻子女妾同補奚官為奴婢。

translations.literal: Mothers, wives, sisters, and those who should be jointly executed in the market—their wives, sons, daughters, and concubines were all assigned as slave girls to the Xi officials.
translations.idiomatic: Mothers, wives, sisters, and others subject to joint execution—their wives, sons, daughters, and concubines were all assigned as slaves to the Xi officials.

sentences.zh: 貲財沒官。

translations.literal: Property and goods were confiscated by the state.
translations.idiomatic: Property was confiscated by the state.

sentences.zh: 劫身皆斬，妻子補兵。

translations.literal: Robbers were all beheaded; wives and children were assigned to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Robbers were beheaded; their wives and children were conscripted into the army.

sentences.zh: 遇赦降死者，黵面為劫字，髠鉗，補冶鎖士終身。

translations.literal: When amnesty reduced death, the face was tattooed with the character for robber, head shaved and cangue applied, assigned as smelting-chain laborers for life.
translations.idiomatic: When amnesty commuted a death sentence, the convict's face was tattooed with the character for robber, his head was shaved and a cangue applied, and he was assigned as a smelting-chain laborer for life.

sentences.zh: 其下又讁運配材官冶士、尚方鎖士，皆以輕重差其年數。

translations.literal: Below that, further reduced to transport and assignment as artisan laborers, smelting laborers, and imperial workshop chain laborers—all according to severity with differences in years.
translations.idiomatic: Lesser sentences were commuted to transport duty or assignment as artisan laborers, smelters, or imperial workshop chain gangs, with terms varying by severity.

sentences.zh: 其重者或終身。

translations.literal: For the most severe, it could be for life.
translations.idiomatic: The most severe cases could mean lifelong servitude.

sentences.zh: 士人有禁錮之科，亦有輕重為差。

translations.literal: For men of letters there was the category of prohibition and confinement, also with light and heavy degrees of difference.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and officials were subject to a category of prohibition and confinement, also graded by severity.

sentences.zh: 其犯清議，則終身不齒。

translations.literal: Those who violated pure reputation were excluded for life.
translations.idiomatic: Those who violated standards of moral reputation were permanently excluded from office.

sentences.zh: 耐罪囚八十已上，十歲已下，及孕者、盲者、侏儒當械繫者，及郡國太守相、都尉、關中侯已上，亭侯已上之父母妻子，及所生坐非死罪除名之罪，二千石已上非檻徵者，並頌繫之。

translations.literal: Service-penalty prisoners eighty and above, ten and below, and pregnant women, the blind, and dwarfs who should wear shackles and cangues, and prefects and chancellors of commanderies and kingdoms, commandants, frontier marquises and above, the parents, wives, and children of marquises and above, and those born to them who committed non-capital offenses of removal from registers, and those of two thousand shi and above not summoned in cages—all were held with red cords.
translations.idiomatic: Service-penalty prisoners aged eighty or above or ten or below, pregnant women, the blind, and dwarfs requiring shackles, prefects and chancellors, commandants, frontier marquises and above, the parents, wives, and children of marquises and above, those born to them guilty of non-capital register offenses, and officials of two thousand shi and above not summoned in cages—all were detained with red cords rather than irons.

sentences.zh: 丹陽尹月一詣建康縣，令三官參共錄獄，察斷枉直。

translations.literal: The Administrator of Danyang once a month went to Jiankang County, ordering the three officials jointly to review cases and examine whether judgments were crooked or straight.
translations.idiomatic: Each month the Administrator of Danyang visited Jiankang County and ordered the three judicial officials jointly to review cases and examine whether judgments were fair.

sentences.zh: 其尚書當錄人之月者，與尚書參共錄之。

translations.literal: Those among the Ministry of Justice who were in the month of reviewing prisoners joined with the Ministry of Justice in jointly reviewing them.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry of Justice officials whose turn it was to review prisoners joined in the joint review.

sentences.zh: 大凡定罪二千五百二十九條。

translations.literal: In general, fixed guilt comprised 2,529 articles.
translations.idiomatic: In all, 2,529 articles defined criminal offenses.

sentences.zh: 二年四月癸卯，法度表上新律，又上令三十卷，科三十卷。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the second year, on the day guimao, Fadu submitted a memorial presenting the new code, and also submitted thirty scrolls of ordinances and thirty scrolls of statutes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of Tianjian 2, on the day guimao, Fadu submitted the new code along with thirty scrolls of ordinances and thirty scrolls of statutes.

sentences.zh: 帝乃以法度守廷尉卿，詔班新律於天下。

translations.literal: The emperor then made Fadu hold the post of Commandant of Justice, and ordered the new code promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Fadu Commandant of Justice and ordered the new code promulgated throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 三年八月，建康女子任提女，坐誘口當死。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year, the Jiankang woman Ren Tinv was guilty of luring people and sentenced to death.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Tianjian 3, a Jiankang woman named Ren Tinv was convicted of abducting people and sentenced to death.

sentences.zh: 其子景慈對鞫辭云，母實行此。

translations.literal: Her son Jingci, facing interrogation, stated in his confession that his mother had indeed done this.
translations.idiomatic: Her son Jingci, under interrogation, confessed that his mother had indeed committed the crime.

sentences.zh: 是時法官虞僧虬啟稱：「案子之事親，有隱無犯，直躬證父，仲尼為非。

translations.literal: At that time the judge Yu Sengqu submitted saying: "In cases of serving one's parents, there is concealment without offense; in straightening one's body to testify against one's father, Confucius deemed it wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Judge Yu Sengqu submitted: "In serving one's parents, concealment is no offense; in testifying against one's father, Confucius deemed it wrong."

sentences.zh: 景慈素無防閑之道，死有明目之據，陷親極刑，傷和損俗。

translations.literal: Jingci throughout lacked the way of proper restraint; in death he had clear evidence in his eyes; he trapped his parent in extreme punishment, harming harmony and damaging custom.
translations.idiomatic: Jingci had never shown proper restraint; he had clear evidence before his eyes yet condemned his mother to death, harming social harmony and damaging public morals.

sentences.zh: 凡乞鞫不審，降罪一等，豈得避五歲之刑，忽死母之命！

translations.literal: Generally, when pleading and interrogating without verification, the punishment is reduced one degree—how could he avoid a five-year sentence yet ignore his mother's life!
translations.idiomatic: When a plea fails verification, the sentence is reduced one degree—how could he evade a five-year term yet deliver his mother to death!

sentences.zh: 景慈宜加罪辟。

translations.literal: Jingci should have additional punishment imposed.
translations.idiomatic: Jingci should receive an aggravated sentence.

sentences.zh: 」詔流于交州。

translations.literal: An edict exiled him to Jiaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict exiled him to Jiaozhou.

sentences.zh: 至是復有流徒之罪。

translations.literal: By this time there was again the offense of exile and transport.
translations.idiomatic: Exile and transport penalties were thus reinstated.

sentences.zh: 其年十月甲子，詔以金作權典，宜在蠲息。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year, on the day jiazi, an edict said that monetary fines as provisional statutes should be suspended.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year, on the day jiazi, an edict declared that monetary fines as provisional statutes should be suspended.

sentences.zh: 於是除贖罪之科。

translations.literal: Thereupon the category of ransom offenses was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The category of redeemable offenses was abolished.

sentences.zh: 武帝敦睦九族，優借朝士，有犯罪者，皆諷羣下，屈法申之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu was affectionate toward the nine clans and showed favor to court officials; when any committed offenses, he always hinted to his subordinates to bend the law in their favor.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu cherished his kinsmen and showed leniency to court officials; when any committed offenses, he always signaled his subordinates to bend the law in their favor.

sentences.zh: 百姓有罪，皆案之以法。

translations.literal: When common people had offenses, all were judged according to the law.
translations.idiomatic: Common people, by contrast, were always judged strictly according to the law.

sentences.zh: 其緣坐則老幼不免，一人亡逃，則舉家質作。

translations.literal: As for joint punishment, the old and young were not exempt; if one person fled, the whole family was held as collateral labor.
translations.idiomatic: Under joint punishment, the elderly and young were not exempt; if one family member fled, the entire household was held as collateral for forced labor.

sentences.zh: 人既窮急，姦宄益深。

translations.literal: People being driven to extremity, treachery and villainy grew deeper.
translations.idiomatic: Driven to desperation, the people turned increasingly to crime.

sentences.zh: 後帝親謁南郊，秣陵老人遮帝曰：「陛下為法，急於黎庶，緩於權貴，非長久之術。

translations.literal: Later when the emperor personally visited the southern suburb, an old man of Moling blocked the emperor saying: "Your Majesty in making law is harsh toward the common people and lenient toward the powerful—this is not a long-term strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the emperor visited the southern suburb, an old man of Moling stopped him and said: "Your Majesty's laws are harsh toward commoners and lenient toward the powerful—this is no strategy for the long term.

sentences.zh: 誠能反是，天下幸甚。

translations.literal: If you can truly reverse this, the realm will be greatly fortunate.
translations.idiomatic: If you can truly reverse this, the realm will be greatly fortunate."

sentences.zh: 」帝於是思有以寬之。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon considered ways to show leniency.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sought ways to show leniency.

sentences.zh: 舊獄法，夫有罪，逮妻子，子有罪，逮父母。

translations.literal: The old prison law: if the husband was guilty, the wife and children were seized; if the son was guilty, the parents were seized.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old prison law, if a husband was guilty his wife and children were seized; if a son was guilty his parents were seized.

sentences.zh: 十一年正月壬辰，乃下詔曰：「自今捕讁之家，及罪應質作，若年有老小者，可停將送。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eleventh year, on the day renchen, an edict was issued saying: "From now on, in families of those arrested for exile, and offenses requiring collateral labor, if there are elderly or young among them, transport may be suspended.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eleventh year, on the day renchen, an edict declared: "From now on, in families of those arrested for exile, and in cases requiring collateral labor, if there are elderly or young among them, transport may be suspended."

sentences.zh: 」十四年，又除黵面之刑。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, tattooing of the face was also abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year, facial tattooing was also abolished.

sentences.zh: 帝銳意儒雅，疎簡刑法，自公卿大臣，咸不以鞫獄留意。

translations.literal: The emperor was keen on Confucian elegance and relaxed in penal law; from dukes and ministers down, none paid attention to trying cases.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor devoted himself to Confucian refinement and relaxed penal enforcement; from dukes and ministers downward, none paid attention to trying cases.

sentences.zh: 姦吏招權，巧文弄法，貨賄成市，多致枉濫。

translations.literal: Corrupt officials grasped power, craftily twisting the law, bribes forming a market, much leading to wrongful conviction.
translations.idiomatic: Corrupt officials grasped power, twisted the law with cunning prose, and bribery flourished, producing many wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 大率二歲刑已上，歲至五千人。

translations.literal: Generally, for punishments of two years and above, each year reached five thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: Generally, sentences of two years or more reached five thousand persons each year.

sentences.zh: 是時徒居作者具五任，其無任者，著斗械。

translations.literal: At that time convicts doing labor service all wore five shackles; those without capacity wore cangue and shackles combined.
translations.idiomatic: At that time convicts in labor service all wore five shackles; those deemed incapable of flight wore combined cangue and shackles.

sentences.zh: 若疾病，權解之。

translations.literal: If ill, they were temporarily released.
translations.idiomatic: If they fell ill, restraints were temporarily removed.

sentences.zh: 是後囚徒或有優劇。

translations.literal: After this, among prisoners there were light and heavy differences.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, prisoners were assigned to light or heavy labor according to circumstances.

sentences.zh: 大同中，皇太子在春宮視事，見而愍之，乃上疏曰：「臣以比時奉勑，權親京師雜事。

translations.literal: In the Datong era, the Crown Prince while in the Eastern Palace attended to affairs, saw this and was moved to pity; he submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant, at this time receiving orders, was temporarily overseeing miscellaneous affairs in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: During the Datong era, the Crown Prince, while attending to affairs in the Eastern Palace, saw this and was moved to pity; he submitted a memorial: "I have lately been ordered to oversee miscellaneous affairs in the capital.

sentences.zh: 切見南北郊壇、材官、車府、太官下省、左裝等處上啟，並請四五歲已下輕囚，助充使役。

translations.literal: I have closely seen the northern and southern suburban altars, artisan offices, carriage depot, imperial kitchen subordinate section, left equipment section, and other places submit requests, all asking for light prisoners of four or five years and below to assist as laborers.
translations.idiomatic: I have seen the northern and southern suburban altars, artisan offices, carriage depot, imperial kitchen, left equipment section, and other offices all request light prisoners of four or five years or less to serve as laborers.

sentences.zh: 自有刑均罪等，愆目不異，而甲付錢署，乙配郊壇。

translations.literal: Although the crime and punishment were equal in grade and the offense was not different, yet A was assigned to the money office and B to the suburban altar.
translations.idiomatic: Although crimes and punishments were equal in grade, one convict might be assigned to the money office while another went to the suburban altar.

sentences.zh: 錢署三所，於事為劇，[6]郊壇六處，在役則優。

translations.literal: The money office had three locations—for the work it was heavy, [6] the suburban altars had six locations—for labor it was light.
translations.idiomatic: The money office had three locations where work was heavy, [6] while the suburban altars had six locations where labor was lighter.

sentences.zh: 今聽獄官詳其可否，舞文之路，自此而生。

translations.literal: Now allowing prison officials to decide what is feasible and infeasible—the path of twisting the text thus arises.
translations.idiomatic: Allowing prison officials to decide what is feasible opens the path to twisting the law.

sentences.zh: 公平難遇其人，流泉易啟其齒，將恐玉科重輕，全關墨綬，金書去取，更由丹筆。

translations.literal: Fairness is hard to find in a person; flowing springs easily open their mouths—I fear the jade code's weight and lightness will entirely depend on the black cord, and gold letters' taking and leaving will further depend on the red brush.
translations.idiomatic: Fairness is hard to find; like flowing springs, corruption easily opens its mouth—I fear the weight of the jade code will entirely depend on the official's black cord, and judicial decisions will further depend on the clerk's red brush.

sentences.zh: 愚謂宜詳立條制，以為永准。

translations.literal: I foolishly consider that detailed regulations should be established as permanent standards.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully suggest that detailed regulations be established as permanent standards.

sentences.zh: 」帝手敕報曰：「頃年已來，處處之役，唯資徒讁，逐急充配。

translations.literal: The emperor wrote a personal reply saying: "In recent years, labor service everywhere relies only on convicts and exiles, urgently filling assignments.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote in reply: "In recent years, labor service everywhere has relied on convicts and exiles, urgently filling assignments.

sentences.zh: 若科制繁細，義同簡絲，切須之處，終不可得。

translations.literal: If the statute system is detailed and fine, the meaning like untangling silk—in places urgently needed, ultimately it cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: If the code is made detailed and fine as untangling silk, what is urgently needed will ultimately be unobtainable.

sentences.zh: 引例興訟，紛紜方始，防杜姦巧，自是為難。

translations.literal: Citing precedents to raise litigation, confusion just beginning—preventing and blocking crafty deception is thereby difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Citing precedents to raise litigation will only breed confusion, and preventing crafty abuse will become difficult.

sentences.zh: 更當別思，取其便也。

translations.literal: We should further think separately and take what is convenient.
translations.idiomatic: We must think further and take what is convenient."

sentences.zh: 」竟弗之從。

translations.literal: In the end he did not follow it.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he did not adopt the proposal.

sentences.zh: 是時王侯子弟皆長，而驕蹇不法。

translations.literal: At that time the sons and younger brothers of kings and marquises had all grown up, yet were arrogant and lawless.
translations.idiomatic: By then the sons and younger brothers of kings and marquises had all come of age, yet remained arrogant and lawless.

sentences.zh: 武帝年老，厭於萬機，又專精佛戒，每斷重罪，則終日弗懌。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu was old, weary of myriad affairs, and also devoted himself exclusively to Buddhist precepts; whenever he passed heavy sentences, he was displeased all day.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu was aging, weary of state affairs, and devoted himself to Buddhist precepts; whenever he passed a heavy sentence, he was displeased all day.

sentences.zh: 嘗遊南苑，臨川王宏，伏人於橋下，將欲為逆。

translations.literal: Once while touring the southern park, Prince Linchuan of the River hid men under the bridge, intending to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Once while touring the southern park, Prince Linchuan of the River hid men under a bridge, intending rebellion.

sentences.zh: 事覺，有司請誅之。

translations.literal: When the matter was discovered, the relevant offices requested execution.
translations.idiomatic: When the plot was discovered, the relevant offices requested execution.

sentences.zh: 帝但泣而讓曰：「我人才十倍於爾，處此恒懷戰懼。

translations.literal: The emperor only wept and reproached him saying: "My talent is ten times yours, yet holding this position I always harbor fear and dread.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor only wept and reproached him: "My talent is ten times yours, yet in this position I always live in fear and dread.

sentences.zh: 爾何為者？

translations.literal: What are you doing?
translations.idiomatic: What are you doing?"

sentences.zh: 我豈不能行周公之事，念汝愚故也。

translations.literal: Could I not do as the Duke of Zhou did? I think of your foolishness, that is all.
translations.idiomatic: "Could I not act as the Duke of Zhou did? I spare you only because you are foolish."

sentences.zh: 」免所居官。

translations.literal: He was removed from his post.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed from his post.

sentences.zh: 頃之，還復本職。

translations.literal: Before long, he was restored to his original post.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, he was restored to his original post.

sentences.zh: 由是王侯驕橫轉甚，或白日殺人於都街，劫賊亡命，咸於王家自匿，薄暮塵起，則剝掠行路，謂之打稽。

translations.literal: From this the kings and marquises grew ever more arrogant; some killed people in broad daylight on the capital streets; bandits and fugitives all hid in princely households; at dusk when dust rose, they plundered travelers on the road—called 'beating the checkpoint.'
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the princes grew ever more arrogant; some killed people in broad daylight on the capital streets; bandits and fugitives all hid in princely households; at dusk they plundered travelers on the roads in what was called 'beating the checkpoint.'

sentences.zh: 武帝深知其弊，而難於誅討。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu deeply knew these abuses, yet found it hard to execute and suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu was well aware of these abuses, yet found it difficult to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 十一年十月，復開贖罪之科。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the eleventh year, the category of ransom offenses was reopened.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the eleventh year, the category of redeemable offenses was reinstated.

sentences.zh: 中大同元年七月甲子，詔自今犯罪，非大逆，父母、祖父母勿坐。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the first year of Zhongdatong, on the day jiazi, an edict said from now on for offenses, unless great treason, parents and grandparents were not jointly punished.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Zhongdatong 1, on the day jiazi, an edict declared that except for great treason, parents and grandparents would no longer be jointly punished.

sentences.zh: 自是禁網漸疎，百姓安之，而貴戚之家，不法尤甚矣。

translations.literal: From this the net of prohibition gradually grew sparse, the common people were at peace, yet among noble clans lawlessness was especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the net of prohibition gradually loosened and common people lived in peace, yet among noble clans lawlessness was especially severe.

sentences.zh: 尋而侯景逆亂。

translations.literal: Before long Hou Jing rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Hou Jing rebelled.

sentences.zh: 陳氏承梁季喪亂，刑典疎闊。

translations.literal: The Chen dynasty inherited the disorders at the end of Liang; the penal code was sparse and loose.
translations.idiomatic: The Chen dynasty inherited the chaos at the end of Liang, under which the penal code had grown sparse and loose.

sentences.zh: 及武帝即位，思革其弊，乃下詔曰：「朕聞唐、虞道盛，設畫象而不犯，夏、商德衰，雖孥戮其未備。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, thinking to reform these abuses, he issued an edict saying: "We have heard that in the flourishing Way of Tang and Yu, painted images were set up yet none transgressed; in the declining virtue of Xia and Shang, even punishing the family was not complete.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, seeking to reform these abuses, he issued an edict: "We have heard that in the flourishing age of Tang and Yu, painted images were set up yet none transgressed; in the declining virtue of Xia and Shang, even family punishment was incomplete.

sentences.zh: 洎乎末代，綱目滋繁，矧屬亂離，憲章遺紊。

translations.literal: Down to the final generations, categories and items grew ever more numerous; moreover belonging to disorder and separation, statutes and regulations were lost and tangled.
translations.idiomatic: By the final generations, legal categories had proliferated; amid disorder and disunion, statutes and regulations were lost and tangled.

sentences.zh: 朕始膺寶曆，思廣政樞，外可搜舉良才，刪改科令，羣僚博議，務存平簡。

translations.literal: We, beginning to receive the imperial calendar, think to extend the pivot of government; externally one may search and recommend worthy talent, revise statutes and ordinances, have the multitude of officials broadly deliberate, striving to preserve fairness and simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: We, having just received the imperial mandate, seek to strengthen governance: worthy talent should be sought, statutes and ordinances revised, and all officials broadly consulted, striving for fairness and simplicity."

sentences.zh: 」於是稍求得梁時明法吏，令與尚書刪定郎范泉，參定律令。

translations.literal: Thereupon they gradually found legal officials from Liang times and ordered them together with Fan Quan, Revising Clerk in the Ministry of Justice, jointly to fix statutes and ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: They gradually found legal officials from Liang times and ordered them, together with Fan Quan, revising clerk in the Ministry of Justice, to codify the statutes and ordinances.

sentences.zh: 又勑尚書僕射沈欽、吏部尚書徐陵、兼尚書左丞宗元饒、兼尚書左丞賀朗參知其事，制律三十卷，令律四十卷。

translations.literal: He also ordered Vice Minister of Justice Shen Qin, Minister of Personnel Xu Ling, Concurrent Vice Director of the Left Section of the Ministry of Justice Zong Yuanrao, and Concurrent Vice Director of the Left Section of the Ministry of Justice He Lang to participate in knowing the matter, fixing thirty scrolls of code and forty scrolls of ordinances.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered Shen Qin, Xu Ling, Zong Yuanrao, and He Lang to participate, producing thirty scrolls of code and forty scrolls of ordinances.

sentences.zh: 採酌前代，條流冗雜，綱目雖多，博而非要。

translations.literal: Drawing from former generations, the items flowed redundantly and complexly; though the categories and items were many, they were broad but not essential.
translations.idiomatic: Drawing on former dynasties, the articles flowed redundantly; though numerous, they were broad without being essential.

sentences.zh: 其制唯重清議禁錮之科。

translations.literal: Its system only emphasized the category of pure reputation and prohibition and confinement.
translations.idiomatic: The code emphasized only the category of moral reputation and prohibition from office.

sentences.zh: 若縉紳之族，犯虧名教，不孝及內亂者，發詔棄之，終身不齒。

translations.literal: If among the gentry clans one violated and damaged name and teaching, unfilial conduct and internal disorder, an edict was issued casting them out, excluded for life.
translations.idiomatic: Gentry who violated moral teaching through unfilial conduct or internal disorder were cast out by edict and permanently excluded from office.

sentences.zh: 先與士人為婚者，許妻家奪之。

translations.literal: Those who had previously contracted marriage with men of letters—the wife's family was permitted to take her back.
translations.idiomatic: If such a person had previously contracted marriage with a scholar, the wife's family was permitted to reclaim her.

sentences.zh: 其獲賊帥及士人惡逆，免死付冶，聽將妻入役，不為年數。

translations.literal: Those who captured bandit chiefs and men of letters guilty of wicked rebellion—death was remitted and they were assigned to smelting work, permitted to bring wives into service, not counted by years.
translations.idiomatic: Those who captured bandit chiefs, and scholars guilty of wicked rebellion, had death remitted and were assigned to smelting work, permitted to bring wives into service without term limits.

sentences.zh: 又存贖罪之律，復父母緣坐之刑。

translations.literal: Also the statute of ransom offenses was retained, and joint punishment of parents was restored.
translations.idiomatic: The statute of redeemable offenses was retained, and joint punishment of parents was restored.

sentences.zh: 自餘篇目條綱，輕重簡繁，一用梁法。

translations.literal: For the remaining chapters, items, and categories, light and heavy, simple and complex—all used Liang law.
translations.idiomatic: For all remaining chapters, articles, and categories, light and heavy, simple and complex—the Liang code was followed throughout.

sentences.zh: 其有贓驗顯然而不款，則上測立。

translations.literal: If there was clear evidence of guilt yet no confession, then standing interrogation was applied.
translations.idiomatic: When guilt was clearly evidenced yet the accused would not confess, standing interrogation was applied.

sentences.zh: 立測者，以土為垛，高一尺，上圓，劣容囚兩足立。

translations.literal: Standing interrogation: earth was piled into a mound one chi high, round on top, barely enough to hold the prisoner's two feet standing.
translations.idiomatic: Standing interrogation required a mound of earth one chi high, rounded on top, barely large enough for the prisoner to stand on both feet.

sentences.zh: 鞭二十，笞三十訖，著兩械及杻，上垛。

translations.literal: After twenty strokes of whip and thirty strokes of rod, both shackles and cangue were applied, and the prisoner mounted the mound.
translations.idiomatic: After twenty strokes of the whip and thirty of the rod, double shackles and a cangue were applied, and the prisoner was placed on the mound.

sentences.zh: 一上測七刻，日再上。

translations.literal: Each mounting lasted seven ke; twice daily they mounted.
translations.idiomatic: Each session on the mound lasted seven ke, twice daily.

sentences.zh: 三七日上測，七日一行鞭。

translations.literal: For three seven-day periods they mounted; every seven days one round of whipping was applied.
translations.idiomatic: They stood on the mound for three seven-day periods, with a whipping every seven days.

sentences.zh: 凡經杖，合一百五十，得度不承者，免死。

translations.literal: Generally, after beatings totaling one hundred fifty strokes, if they reached the limit yet still did not confess, death was remitted.
translations.idiomatic: After one hundred fifty strokes in all, if the prisoner still would not confess, the death sentence was commuted.

sentences.zh: 其髠鞭五歲刑，降死一等，鎖二重。

translations.literal: For shaved head and whip five-year punishment, death was reduced one degree, with double chains.
translations.idiomatic: Shaved head and five-year term with whipping reduced a death sentence one degree and required double chains.

sentences.zh: [7]其五歲刑已下，並鎖一重。

translations.literal: [7] For five-year punishment and below, all wore single chains.
translations.idiomatic: [7] Sentences of five years or less required single chains.

sentences.zh: 五歲四歲刑，若有官，准當二年，餘並居作。

translations.literal: For five-year and four-year punishment, if one held office, two years were commuted by rank; the remainder was served as labor.
translations.idiomatic: For four- and five-year terms, officials could commute two years by rank; the remainder was served as labor.

sentences.zh: 其三歲刑，若有官，准當二年，餘一年贖。

translations.literal: For three-year punishment, if one held office, two years were commuted by rank; the remaining one year was redeemed.
translations.idiomatic: For three-year terms, officials could commute two years by rank; the remaining year could be redeemed.

sentences.zh: 若公坐過誤，罰金。

translations.literal: If through public office one sat in error through mistake, monetary fine.
translations.idiomatic: Officials guilty of negligent error in public duty paid monetary fines.

sentences.zh: 其二歲刑，有官者，贖論。

translations.literal: For two-year punishment, those with office were judged according to ransom.
translations.idiomatic: Two-year terms for officials were subject to redemption.

sentences.zh: 一歲刑，無官亦贖論。

translations.literal: For one-year punishment, even those without office were judged according to ransom.
translations.idiomatic: One-year terms could be redeemed even by those without office.

sentences.zh: 寒庶人，准決鞭杖。

translations.literal: Common people of humble status were permitted whip and cudgel sentences.
translations.idiomatic: Commoners of humble status received whip and cudgel penalties as prescribed.

sentences.zh: 囚並著械，徒並著鎖，不計階品。

translations.literal: Prisoners all wore shackles, convicts all wore chains, regardless of rank grade.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners wore shackles and convicts wore chains regardless of rank.

sentences.zh: [8]死罪將決，乘露車，著三械，加壺手。

translations.literal: [8] When capital punishment was about to be decided, they rode in an open cart, wore three shackles, and had hand restraints added.
translations.idiomatic: [8] Condemned prisoners rode in an open cart wearing three shackles plus hand restraints.

sentences.zh: 至市，脫手械及壺手焉。

translations.literal: Upon reaching the market, hand shackles and hand restraints were removed.
translations.idiomatic: At the execution ground, hand shackles and restraints were removed.

sentences.zh: 當刑於市者，夜須明，雨須晴。

translations.literal: When punishment was to be carried out in the market, night required brightness and rain required clear weather.
translations.idiomatic: Market executions required daylight and clear weather.

sentences.zh: 晦朔、八節、六齊、月在張心日，並不得行刑。

translations.literal: New and full moon, the eight seasonal nodes, the six fast days, and days when the moon was in the heart of Zhang—all were forbidden for carrying out punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Executions were forbidden on new and full moons, the eight seasonal nodes, the six fast days, and days when the moon was in the Heart of Zhang.

sentences.zh: 廷尉寺為北獄，建康縣為南獄，並置正監平。

translations.literal: The Court of the Commandant of Justice was the northern prison, Jiankang County the southern prison; both had chief wardens and assessors appointed.
translations.idiomatic: The Commandant of Justice's court served as the northern prison and Jiankang County as the southern prison; both had chief wardens and assessors.

sentences.zh: 又制，常以三月，侍中、吏部尚書、尚書、三公郎、部都令史、三公錄寃局，令史、御史中丞、侍御史、蘭臺令史，親行京師諸獄及冶署，理察囚徒寃枉。

translations.literal: It was also regulated that regularly in the third month, the Palace Attendant, Minister of Personnel, Ministers of Justice, gentlemen of the Three Excellencies, chief clerks of sections, clerks of the Three Excellencies' wrongful-conviction review office, Imperial Censor, Attending Censor, and clerks of the Orchid Terrace personally inspected all capital prisons and smelting offices, examining whether prisoners had been wrongfully convicted.
translations.idiomatic: Each third month, the Palace Attendant, Minister of Personnel, Ministers of Justice, Three Excellencies' staff, chief clerks, wrongful-conviction review clerks, Imperial Censor, Attending Censor, and Orchid Terrace clerks personally inspected all capital prisons and smelting offices to examine wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 文帝性明察，留心刑政，親覽獄訟，督責羣下，政號嚴明。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen was by nature clear-sighted, attentive to penal administration, personally reviewing lawsuits, supervising and holding subordinates accountable—his government was called strict and bright.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen was clear-sighted and attentive to penal matters, personally reviewing lawsuits and holding officials accountable—his reign was known for strict and fair justice.

sentences.zh: 是時承寬政之後，功臣貴戚有非法，帝咸以法繩之，頗號峻刻。

translations.literal: At that time, inheriting after lenient government, when meritorious ministers and noble kin acted unlawfully, the emperor always bound them with the law—he was quite called harsh and severe.
translations.idiomatic: Following an era of leniency, when meritorious ministers and noble kin broke the law, Emperor Wen always held them to account—earning a reputation for severity.

sentences.zh: 及宣帝即位，優借文武之士，崇簡易之政，上下便之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan ascended the throne, he showed favor to civil and military scholars and honored a simple and easy government—above and below found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, he favored civil and military scholars and promoted simple governance that benefited all ranks.

sentences.zh: 其後政令既寬，刑法不立，又以連年北伐，疲人聚為劫盜矣。

translations.literal: Afterward, as government orders grew lenient and penal law was not enforced, and with consecutive years of northern campaigns, exhausted people gathered as bandits and robbers.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, as governance grew lax and penal law went unenforced, and with years of northern campaigns exhausting the people, banditry flourished.

sentences.zh: 後主即位，信任讒邪，羣下縱恣，鬻獄成市，賞罰之命，不出于外。

translations.literal: When the Later Lord ascended the throne, he trusted slanderers and the wicked; subordinates indulged themselves freely; selling judgments formed a market; orders of reward and punishment did not issue from outside.
translations.idiomatic: When the Later Lord took the throne, he trusted slanderers; officials ran wild; justice was sold openly; and rewards and punishments were decided entirely within the palace.

sentences.zh: 後主性猜忍疾忌，威令不行，左右有忤意者，動至夷戮。

translations.literal: The Later Lord was by nature suspicious, cruel, quick to envy, and his authority and commands did not prevail; those around him who displeased him were often exterminated to the last.
translations.idiomatic: The Later Lord was suspicious, cruel, and jealous; his authority went unheeded; those who displeased him were often exterminated to the last.

sentences.zh: 百姓怨叛，以至於滅。

translations.literal: The common people resented and rebelled, leading to destruction.
translations.idiomatic: The people rose in resentment and rebellion, leading to the dynasty's destruction.

sentences.zh: 齊神武、文襄，並由魏相，尚用舊法。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenwu and Wenxiang of Qi both came from Wei chancellorships and still used the old law.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenwu and Wenxiang of Northern Qi, both former Wei chancellors, continued to use the old Wei code.

sentences.zh: 及文宣天保元年，始命羣官刊定魏朝麟趾格。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenxuan in the first year of Tianbao first ordered the multitude of officials to revise and fix the Wei dynasty's Linzhi Code.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 1, Emperor Wenxuan first ordered officials to revise the Wei dynasty's Linzhi Code.

sentences.zh: 是時軍國多事，政刑不一，決獄定罪，罕依律文，相承謂之變法從事。

translations.literal: At that time military and state affairs were many, government and punishment were not unified, deciding cases and fixing guilt rarely followed the text of the code—what was handed down was called 'changing the law to handle matters.'
translations.idiomatic: Military and state affairs were pressing, government and punishment lacked unity, and judgments rarely followed the code—what passed for law was called 'changing the law to handle matters.'

sentences.zh: 清河房超為黎陽郡守，有趙道德者，使以書屬超。

translations.literal: Fang Chao of Qinghe was Administrator of Liyang Commandery; there was one Zhao Daode who sent a letter entrusting matters to Chao.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Chao of Qinghe was Administrator of Liyang; one Zhao Daode sent him a letter requesting a favor.

sentences.zh: 超不發書，棒殺其使。

translations.literal: Chao did not release the letter and beat the messenger to death.
translations.idiomatic: Chao refused the letter and beat the messenger to death.

sentences.zh: 文宣於是令守宰各設棒，以誅屬請之使。

translations.literal: Wenxuan thereupon ordered each prefect and magistrate to set up cudgels to execute messengers making entreaties on others' behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan then ordered every prefect and magistrate to set up cudgels for executing messengers who came soliciting favors.

sentences.zh: 後都官郎中宋軌奏曰：「昔曹操懸棒，威於亂時，今施之太平，未見其可。

translations.literal: Later Langzhong of the Capital Office Song Gui submitted saying: "Formerly Cao Cao hung up cudgels, awe-inspiring in chaotic times; now applying them in peace, I do not see that it is feasible.
translations.idiomatic: Later Song Gui of the Capital Office submitted: "Cao Cao hung up cudgels to inspire awe in chaotic times; applying them in peacetime seems inadvisable.

sentences.zh: 若受使請賕，猶致大戮，身為枉法，何以加罪？
