translations.literal: If a messenger accepts entreaties and solicits bribes, he still receives great execution—if the body itself bends the law, how can punishment be added?
translations.idiomatic: If a messenger solicits bribes, he already faces execution—if the official himself bends the law, how can further punishment be added?"

sentences.zh: 」於是罷之。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The practice was abolished.

sentences.zh: 既而司徒功曹張老上書，稱大齊受命已來，律令未改，非所以創制垂法，革人視聽。

translations.literal: Before long Zhang Lao, Functionary of the Ministry of Education, submitted a memorial saying that since Great Qi received the mandate, statutes and ordinances had not been changed—this was not the way to create institutions and hand down law, reforming people's sight and hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Zhang Lao of the Ministry of Education submitted that since Great Qi received the mandate, statutes and ordinances had not been revised—hardly the way to establish institutions and reform public expectations.

sentences.zh: 於是始命羣官，議造齊律，積年不成。

translations.literal: Thereupon he first ordered the multitude of officials to deliberate on creating Qi law; accumulated over years without completion.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were then ordered to draft a Qi code, but years passed without completion.

sentences.zh: 其決獄猶依魏舊。

translations.literal: Deciding cases still followed Wei precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Case decisions still followed Wei precedent.

sentences.zh: 是時刑政尚新，吏皆奉法。

translations.literal: At that time penal government was still fresh, and officials all upheld the law.
translations.idiomatic: At first penal administration was still fresh, and officials upheld the law.

sentences.zh: 自六年之後，帝遂以功業自矜，恣行酷暴，昏狂酗醟，任情喜怒。

translations.literal: From after the sixth year, the emperor then prided himself on his achievements, at will practicing cruel violence, benighted, mad, drunk, and debauched, following his emotions in likes and dislikes.
translations.idiomatic: After the sixth year, the emperor grew proud of his achievements and practiced cruel violence at will—benighted, drunken, and debauched, indulging every whim.

sentences.zh: 為大鑊、長鋸、剉碓之屬，並陳於庭，意有不快，則手自屠裂，或命左右臠噉，以逞其意。

translations.literal: Great cauldrons, long saws, grinding pestles, and the like were all displayed in the courtyard; when displeased, he personally butchered and tore apart, or ordered those around him to carve and devour, to satisfy his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Great cauldrons, long saws, and grinding pestles were displayed in the courtyard; when displeased, he personally butchered victims or ordered attendants to carve and devour them to satisfy his cruelty.

sentences.zh: 時僕射楊遵彥，乃令憲司先定死罪囚，置于仗衞之中，帝欲殺人，則執以應命，謂之供御囚。

translations.literal: At that time Vice Director Yang Zunyan ordered the censorate first to fix death-sentence prisoners and place them among the armed guards; when the emperor wished to kill, they were seized to answer the command—called 'prisoners supplied for the emperor.'
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Yang Zunyan ordered the censorate to keep condemned prisoners among the armed guards; when the emperor wished to kill, one was produced on command—these were called 'prisoners supplied for the emperor.'

sentences.zh: 經三月不殺者，則免其死。

translations.literal: If after three months they were not killed, then their death was remitted.
translations.idiomatic: If not executed within three months, the death sentence was remitted.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗幸金鳳臺，受佛戒，多召死囚，編籧篨為翅，命之飛下，謂之放生。

translations.literal: The emperor once visited the Golden Phoenix Tower, received Buddhist precepts, summoned many death-sentence prisoners, wove bamboo mats as wings, and ordered them to fly down—called ' releasing life.'
translations.idiomatic: Once at the Golden Phoenix Tower, after receiving Buddhist precepts, he summoned condemned prisoners, fitted them with woven bamboo wings, and ordered them to fly down—calling it ' releasing life.'

sentences.zh: 墜皆致死，帝視以為歡笑。

translations.literal: All who fell died; the emperor watched and took it as merriment.
translations.idiomatic: All who fell died; the emperor watched and laughed.

sentences.zh: 時有司折獄，又皆酷法。

translations.literal: At that time the relevant offices judging cases again all used cruel law.
translations.idiomatic: Judicial offices again applied cruel methods in trying cases.

sentences.zh: 訊囚則用車輻𤠮杖，夾指壓踝，又立之燒犁耳上，或使以臂貫燒車釭。

translations.literal: Interrogating prisoners used wagon-spoke cudgels, finger-crushing and ankle-pressing, also standing them on burning plowshares by the ears, or making them pass their arms through burning wagon axles.
translations.idiomatic: Interrogation employed wagon-spoke cudgels, finger-crushing and ankle-pressing, standing prisoners on burning plowshares, or forcing arms through burning wagon axles.

sentences.zh: 既不勝其苦，皆致誣伏。

translations.literal: Unable to bear the suffering, all led to false confession.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to bear the suffering, all confessed falsely.

sentences.zh: 七年，豫州檢使白𢶏，為左丞盧斐所劾，乃於獄中誣告斐受金。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, the Yuzhou inspector Bai Kai was impeached by Vice Director Lu Fei; he then in prison falsely accused Fei of accepting gold.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, Yuzhou inspector Bai Kai, impeached by Vice Director Lu Fei, falsely accused Fei in prison of accepting bribes.

sentences.zh: 文宣知其姦罔，詔令按之，果無其事。

translations.literal: Wenxuan knew his deceit and falsehood, ordered investigation, and indeed there was no such matter.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan knew the accusation was false, ordered investigation, and found no basis for it.

sentences.zh: 乃勑八座議立案劾格，負罪不得告人事。

translations.literal: He then ordered the Eight Seats to deliberate and establish a precedent for impeachment, that those guilty of offenses could not accuse others.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the Eight Seats to establish a precedent that the guilty could not accuse others.

sentences.zh: 於是挾姦者畏糾，乃先加誣訟，以擬當格，吏不能斷。

translations.literal: Thereupon those harboring wickedness feared prosecution and first added false accusations to meet the precedent; officials could not decide.
translations.idiomatic: Those harboring guilt then preemptively filed false accusations to exploit the precedent, leaving officials unable to decide.

sentences.zh: 又妄相引，大獄動至千人，多移歲月。

translations.literal: Also falsely implicating one another, great prisons often reached a thousand persons, often extending over many months.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners falsely implicated one another; major cases often involved a thousand persons and dragged on for months.

sentences.zh: 然帝猶委政輔臣楊遵彥，彌縫其闕，故時議者竊云，主昏於上，政清於下。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor still entrusted government to the assisting minister Yang Zunyan, who patched its gaps; therefore contemporary opinion secretly said: the ruler was benighted above, yet government was clear below.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the emperor still entrusted governance to Yang Zunyan, who patched the system's gaps; contemporaries whispered that the ruler was benighted above while government remained clear below.

sentences.zh: 孝昭在藩，已知其失，即位之後，將加懲革。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozhao, while still in his princely fief, already knew these faults; after ascending the throne, he intended to add punishment and reform.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhao, while still a prince, already knew these faults; upon taking the throne he intended reform.

sentences.zh: 未幾而崩。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died.

sentences.zh: 武成即位，思存輕典，大寧元年，乃下詔曰：「王者所用，唯在賞罰，賞貴適理，罰在得情。

translations.literal: Emperor Wucheng ascended the throne, thinking to preserve lenient statutes; in the first year of Daning, he issued an edict saying: "What the king employs is only in reward and punishment; reward values appropriateness to reason, punishment lies in obtaining the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wucheng, seeking lenient statutes, issued an edict in Daning 1: "A king's tools are reward and punishment alone; reward must fit the merit, punishment must fit the crime.

sentences.zh: 然理容進退，事涉疑似，盟府司勳，或有開塞之路，三尺律令，未窮畫一之道。

translations.literal: Yet reason permits advance and retreat; matters involve suspicion; the covenant house and merit office may have paths of opening and closing; the three-chi statutes and ordinances have not exhausted the way of uniform application.
translations.idiomatic: Yet reason allows discretion; cases involve doubt; merit offices may open or close paths; and the written code cannot exhaust every circumstance.

sentences.zh: 想文王之官人，念宣尼之止訟，刑賞之宜，思獲其所。

translations.literal: Thinking of King Wen's appointing men, recalling Confucius's stopping litigation—the appropriateness of punishment and reward, thinking to obtain their proper place.
translations.idiomatic: Recalling King Wen's appointment of men and Confucius's counsel against litigation, we seek the proper measure of punishment and reward.

sentences.zh: 自今諸應賞罰，皆賞疑從重，罰疑從輕。

translations.literal: From now on for all who should receive reward or punishment, when reward is doubtful apply the heavier, when punishment is doubtful apply the lighter.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, when reward is doubtful apply the greater, when punishment is doubtful apply the lesser."

sentences.zh: 」又以律令不成，頻加催督。

translations.literal: Also because statutes and ordinances were not completed, he frequently added urging and supervision.
translations.idiomatic: Because the code remained unfinished, he frequently urged its completion.

sentences.zh: 河清三年，尚書令、趙郡王叡等，奏上齊律十二篇：一曰名例，二曰禁衞，三日婚戶，四曰擅興，五曰違制，六曰詐偽，七曰鬬訟，八曰賊盜，九曰捕斷，十曰毀損，十一曰廐牧，十二曰雜。

translations.literal: In the third year of Heqing, Minister of Justice, Prince Rui of Zhao Commandery, and others submitted the Qi code in twelve chapters: first, Names and Examples; second, Forbidden Guard; third, Marriage and Households; fourth, Unauthorized Mobilization; fifth, Violating Regulations; sixth, Fraud and Forgery; seventh, Fighting and Litigation; eighth, Bandits and Robbers; ninth, Pursuit and Judgment; tenth, Destruction and Damage; eleventh, Stables and Herds; twelfth, Miscellaneous.
translations.idiomatic: In Heqing 3, Prince Rui of Zhao and others submitted the Qi code in twelve chapters: Names and Examples, Forbidden Guard, Marriage and Households, Unauthorized Mobilization, Violating Regulations, Fraud and Forgery, Fighting and Litigation, Bandits and Robbers, Pursuit and Judgment, Destruction and Damage, Stables and Herds, and Miscellaneous.

sentences.zh: 其定罪九百四十九條。

translations.literal: Fixed guilt comprised 949 articles.
translations.idiomatic: Criminal offenses were defined in 949 articles.

sentences.zh: 又上新令四十卷，大抵採魏、晉故事。

translations.literal: Also submitted new ordinances in forty scrolls, generally drawing on Wei and Jin precedents.
translations.idiomatic: They also submitted forty scrolls of new ordinances, generally drawn from Wei and Jin precedents.

sentences.zh: 其制，刑名五：一曰死，重者轘之，其次梟首，並陳屍三日；

translations.literal: Its system had five punishment names: first, death—for the severe, dismemberment at the waist; next, exposing the head; both with corpse displayed three days;
translations.idiomatic: Five categories of punishment were established: first, death—for the most severe, dismemberment at the waist; next, exposing the head; both with the corpse displayed for three days;

sentences.zh: 無市者，列於鄉亭顯處。

translations.literal: where there was no market, displayed at a conspicuous place in village or pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: where no market existed, at a conspicuous place in village or pavilion.

sentences.zh: 其次斬刑，殊身首。

translations.literal: Next, decapitation, separating body and head.
translations.idiomatic: Next came decapitation, separating body and head.

sentences.zh: 其次絞刑，死而不殊。

translations.literal: Next, strangulation—death without separation.
translations.idiomatic: Next came strangulation—death without dismemberment.

sentences.zh: 凡四等。

translations.literal: In all four degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Four degrees in all.

sentences.zh: 二曰流刑，謂論犯可死，原情可降，鞭笞各一百，髠之，投于邊裔，以為兵卒。

translations.literal: Second, exile punishment—meaning judged guilty of what could be death, considering circumstances it could be reduced, one hundred strokes each of whip and rod, head shaved, cast to the border regions to serve as soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Second, exile—for offenses warranting death but reducible in circumstance: one hundred strokes each of whip and rod, head shaved, and exile to the frontier as a soldier.

sentences.zh: 未有道里之差。

translations.literal: There was not yet difference in distance.
translations.idiomatic: No gradations of distance were yet prescribed.

sentences.zh: 其不合遠配者，男子長徒，女子配舂，並六年。

translations.literal: Those not suited to distant assignment—men long-term convict labor, women assigned to pounding grain—both six years.
translations.idiomatic: Those not suited to distant exile—men to long-term convict labor, women to pounding grain—both for six years.

sentences.zh: 三曰刑罪，即耐罪也。

translations.literal: Third, punishment offense—that is, service penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Third, penal servitude—that is, service penalties.

sentences.zh: 有五歲、四歲、三歲、二歲、一歲之差。

translations.literal: There were differences of five years, four years, three years, two years, and one year.
translations.idiomatic: Terms ranged from five years down to one year.

sentences.zh: 凡五等。

translations.literal: Five degrees in all.
translations.idiomatic: Five degrees in all.

sentences.zh: 各加鞭一百。

translations.literal: Each added one hundred strokes of whip.
translations.idiomatic: Each added one hundred strokes of the whip.

sentences.zh: 其五歲者，又加笞八十，四歲者六十，三歲者四十，二歲者二十，一歲者無笞。

translations.literal: For five-year terms, additionally eighty rod strokes; four-year, sixty; three-year, forty; two-year, twenty; one-year, no rod strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Five-year terms added eighty rod strokes; four-year, sixty; three-year, forty; two-year, twenty; one-year, none.

sentences.zh: 並鎖輸左校而不髠。

translations.literal: All were chained and sent to the left work camp without shaving the head.
translations.idiomatic: All were chained and sent to the left work camp without shaving the head.

sentences.zh: 無保者鉗之。

translations.literal: Those without guarantors were cangue-applied.
translations.idiomatic: Those without guarantors wore the cangue.

sentences.zh: 婦人配舂及掖庭織。

translations.literal: Women were assigned to pounding grain and palace weaving.
translations.idiomatic: Women were assigned to pounding grain and palace weaving.

sentences.zh: 四曰鞭，有一百、八十、六十、五十、四十之差，凡五等。

translations.literal: Fourth, whip—with differences of one hundred, eighty, sixty, fifty, and forty; five degrees in all.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, the whip—one hundred, eighty, sixty, fifty, and forty strokes; five degrees in all.

sentences.zh: 五曰杖，有三十、二十、十之差，凡三等。

translations.literal: Fifth, cudgel—with differences of thirty, twenty, and ten; three degrees in all.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, the cudgel—thirty, twenty, and ten strokes; three degrees in all.

sentences.zh: 大凡為十五等。

translations.literal: In general there were fifteen degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Fifteen degrees in all.

sentences.zh: 當加者上就次，當減者下就次。

translations.literal: When increasing, go up to the next degree; when decreasing, go down to the next degree.
translations.idiomatic: When aggravating, apply the next higher degree; when mitigating, the next lower.

sentences.zh: 贖罪舊以金，皆代以中絹。

translations.literal: Ransom offenses formerly used gold; all were replaced with medium-grade silk.
translations.idiomatic: Redemption formerly paid in gold was replaced with medium-grade silk.

sentences.zh: 死一百匹，流九十二匹，刑五歲七十八匹，四歲六十四匹，三歲五十匹，二歲三十六匹。

translations.literal: Death one hundred bolts, exile ninety-two bolts, five-year term seventy-eight bolts, four-year sixty-four bolts, three-year fifty bolts, two-year thirty-six bolts.
translations.idiomatic: Death required one hundred bolts, exile ninety-two, five-year terms seventy-eight, four-year sixty-four, three-year fifty, two-year thirty-six.

sentences.zh: 各通鞭笞論。

translations.literal: Each included whip and rod strokes in the calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Whip and rod strokes were included in each calculation.

sentences.zh: 一歲無笞，則通鞭二十四匹。

translations.literal: One-year term without rod strokes then included whip for twenty-four bolts.
translations.idiomatic: One-year terms without rod strokes required twenty-four bolts including the whip.

sentences.zh: 鞭杖每十，贖絹一匹。

translations.literal: For every ten strokes of whip or cudgel, one bolt of silk for ransom.
translations.idiomatic: Every ten strokes of whip or cudgel required one bolt of silk for redemption.

sentences.zh: 至鞭百，則絹十匹。

translations.literal: Up to one hundred strokes of whip, then ten bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred whip strokes required ten bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 無絹之鄉，皆准絹收錢。

translations.literal: Districts without silk all converted silk to cash collection.
translations.idiomatic: Districts without silk collected cash equivalent to the silk value.

sentences.zh: 自贖笞十已上至死，又為十五等之差。

translations.literal: From redeeming ten rod strokes and above up to death, again there were fifteen degrees of difference.
translations.idiomatic: From redeeming ten rod strokes upward through death, fifteen degrees of redemption were again established.

sentences.zh: 當加減次，如正決法。

translations.literal: When increasing or decreasing degrees, follow the method of regular judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Increases and decreases followed the method of regular sentencing.

sentences.zh: 合贖者，謂流內官及爵秩比視、老小閹癡并過失之屬。

translations.literal: Those eligible for ransom meant officials within exile, and those of rank and salary equivalent, the old and young, eunuchs, idiots, and the category of negligence and error.
translations.idiomatic: Those eligible for redemption included officials subject to exile, those of equivalent rank and salary, the old and young, eunuchs, idiots, and negligent offenders.

sentences.zh: 犯罰絹一匹及杖十已上，皆名為罪人。

translations.literal: Those committing punishment of one bolt of silk and cudgel strokes of ten and above were all called criminals.
translations.idiomatic: Offenders subject to one bolt of silk or ten cudgel strokes and above were all classified as criminals.

sentences.zh: 盜及殺人而亡者，即懸名注籍，甄其一房配驛戶。

translations.literal: Those who robbed or killed and fled had their names posted on registers; one branch of the clan was selected and assigned as courier households.
translations.idiomatic: Robbers and murderers who fled had their names posted; one branch of the clan was assigned as courier households.

sentences.zh: 宗室則不注盜，及不入奚官，不加宮刑。

translations.literal: Imperial clansmen were not posted for robbery, nor entered Xi offices, nor received palace punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansmen were not posted for robbery, not assigned to Xi offices, and not subject to palace punishment.

sentences.zh: [9]自犯流罪已下合贖者，及婦人犯刑已下，侏儒、篤疾、癃殘非犯死罪，皆頌繫之。

translations.literal: [9] From those guilty of exile and below eligible for ransom, and women guilty of penal servitude and below, dwarfs, seriously ill, crippled and disabled not guilty of capital crimes—all were held with red cords.
translations.idiomatic: [9] Those guilty of exile or less eligible for redemption, women guilty of penal servitude or less, dwarfs, the seriously ill, and the crippled not guilty of capital crimes—all were detained with red cords.

sentences.zh: 罪刑年者鎖，無鎖以枷。

translations.literal: Those with penal terms by year wore chains; without chains, a cangue.
translations.idiomatic: Year-term convicts wore chains; without chains, a cangue.

sentences.zh: 流罪已上加杻械。

translations.literal: For exile and above, cangue and shackles were added.
translations.idiomatic: Exile and above required cangue and shackles.

sentences.zh: 死罪者桁之。

translations.literal: Those guilty of capital crimes wore the yoke.
translations.idiomatic: Condemned prisoners wore the yoke.

sentences.zh: 決流刑鞭笞者，鞭其背。

translations.literal: When deciding exile punishment with whip and rod, the back was whipped.
translations.idiomatic: In exile sentences involving whip and rod, the back was whipped.

sentences.zh: 五十，一易執鞭人。

translations.literal: At fifty strokes, the whip-bearer was changed once.
translations.idiomatic: The whip-bearer was changed every fifty strokes.

sentences.zh: 鞭鞘皆用熟皮，削去廉稜。

translations.literal: Whip handles all used tanned hide, with the grain edge shaved off.
translations.idiomatic: Whip handles were all of tanned hide with the smooth edge shaved away.

sentences.zh: 鞭瘡長一尺。

translations.literal: The whip lash was one chi long.
translations.idiomatic: The whip lash was one chi in length.

sentences.zh: 笞者笞臀，而不中易人。

translations.literal: Rod strokes struck the buttocks, and the bearer was not changed midway.
translations.idiomatic: Rod strokes struck the buttocks, without changing the bearer midway.

sentences.zh: 杖長三尺五寸，大頭徑二分半，小頭徑一分半。

translations.literal: Cudgels were three chi five cun long, the large end two and a half fen in diameter, the small end one and a half fen.
translations.idiomatic: Cudgels were three chi five cun long, two and a half fen thick at the large end and one and a half fen at the small end.

sentences.zh: 決三十已下杖者，長四尺，大頭徑三分，小頭徑二分。

translations.literal: For cudgel sentences of thirty and below, length was four chi, large end three fen in diameter, small end two fen.
translations.idiomatic: Cudgels for sentences of thirty strokes or less were four chi long, three fen thick at the large end and two fen at the small end.

sentences.zh: 在官犯罪，鞭杖十為一負。

translations.literal: For offenses committed while in office, ten strokes of whip or cudgel counted as one demerit.
translations.idiomatic: For officials committing offenses, ten strokes of whip or cudgel counted as one demerit.

sentences.zh: 閑局六負為一殿，平局八負為一殿，繁局十負為一殿。

translations.literal: Leisure bureaus: six demerits equaled one dismissal; ordinary bureaus: eight demerits; busy bureaus: ten demerits.
translations.idiomatic: Leisure bureaus required six demerits for dismissal, ordinary bureaus eight, and busy bureaus ten.

sentences.zh: 加於殿者，復計為負焉。

translations.literal: When exceeding dismissal, it was again calculated as demerits.
translations.idiomatic: Penalties beyond dismissal were again calculated in demerits.

sentences.zh: 赦日，則武庫令設金雞及鼓於閶闔門外之右。

translations.literal: On amnesty days, the Director of the Armory set up the golden rooster and drum to the right outside the Changhe Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On amnesty days, the Director of the Armory set up the golden rooster and drum to the right outside the Changhe Gate.

sentences.zh: 勒集囚徒於闕前，撾鼓千聲，釋枷鎖焉。

translations.literal: Prisoners were assembled before the palace gate; the drum was beaten a thousand times and shackles released.
translations.idiomatic: Prisoners were assembled before the palace; the drum was beaten a thousand times and shackles were released.

sentences.zh: 又列重罪十條：一曰反逆，二曰大逆，三曰叛，四曰降，五曰惡逆，六曰不道，七曰不敬，八曰不孝，九曰不義，十曰內亂。

translations.literal: Also listed were ten grave offenses: first, rebellion; second, great treason; third, defection; fourth, surrender; fifth, wicked treason; sixth, unnatural conduct; seventh, disrespect; eighth, unfilial conduct; ninth, unrighteous conduct; tenth, internal disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Ten grave offenses were also listed: rebellion, great treason, defection, surrender, wicked treason, unnatural conduct, disrespect, unfilial conduct, unrighteous conduct, and internal disorder.

sentences.zh: 其犯此十者，不在八議論贖之限。

translations.literal: Those who committed these ten were not within the limits of the eight deliberations or ransom discussion.
translations.idiomatic: Those who committed these ten offenses were excluded from the eight deliberations and redemption.

sentences.zh: 是後法令明審，科條簡要，又勑仕門之子弟，常講習之。

translations.literal: After this, statutes and ordinances were clear and bright, articles concise; also ordered sons and younger brothers of official families to regularly study them.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter statutes were clear and articles concise; sons of official families were ordered to study them regularly.

sentences.zh: 齊人多曉法律，蓋由此也。

translations.literal: Qi people widely understood the law—likely because of this.
translations.idiomatic: Northern Qi people widely understood the law, largely because of this.

sentences.zh: 其不可為定法者，別制權令二卷，與之並行。

translations.literal: What could not be made fixed law was separately compiled as provisional ordinances in two scrolls, running parallel with it.
translations.idiomatic: Matters that could not be fixed as permanent law were compiled separately as provisional ordinances in two scrolls, running parallel with the code.

sentences.zh: 後平秦王高歸彥謀反，須有約罪，律無正條，於是遂有別條權格，與律並行。

translations.literal: Later when Prince Ping of Qin, Gao Guiyan, plotted rebellion, there needed to be stipulated guilt, but the code had no proper article; thereupon there were separate provisional articles, running parallel with the code.
translations.idiomatic: Later when Prince Ping of Qin, Gao Guiyan, plotted rebellion, no proper code article existed; separate provisional articles were therefore enacted alongside the code.

sentences.zh: 大理明法，上下比附，欲出則附依輕議，欲入則附從重法，姦吏因之，舞文出沒。

translations.literal: The Court of Justice understood the law; above and below they analogized—wishing to reduce, they analogized to lighter deliberation; wishing to increase, they analogized to heavier law; corrupt officials thereby twisted the text in and out.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Justice applied analogical reasoning—reducing sentences by lighter precedents, increasing by heavier ones—giving corrupt officials room to twist the law.

sentences.zh: 至于後主，權幸用事，有不附之者，陰中以法。

translations.literal: As for the Later Lord, favorites wielded power; those who did not attach to them were secretly struck with the law.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Later Lord, favorites wielded power; those who did not attach to them were secretly prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 綱紀紊亂，卒至於亡。

translations.literal: Discipline and order were tangled and confused, ultimately leading to destruction.
translations.idiomatic: Discipline collapsed, ultimately leading to the dynasty's destruction.

sentences.zh: 周文帝之有關中也，霸業初基，典章多闕。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou held the Guanzhong region, his hegemonic enterprise was just beginning and institutions were largely lacking.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Zhou held the Guanzhong region, his hegemony was just beginning and institutions were largely lacking.

sentences.zh: 大統元年，命有司斟酌今古通變，可以益時者，為二十四條之制，奏之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong, he ordered the relevant offices to consider past and present with flexible adaptation, what could benefit the times, making a system of twenty-four articles, and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong 1, he ordered officials to adapt past and present for the times, producing a twenty-four-article system.

sentences.zh: 七年，又下十二條制。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, twelve more articles were issued.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, twelve more articles were issued.

sentences.zh: 十年，魏帝命尚書蘇綽，總三十六條，更損益為五卷，班於天下。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, the Wei emperor ordered Minister of Justice Su Chuo to compile the thirty-six articles, further adding and reducing to five scrolls, and promulgated them throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, the Wei emperor ordered Su Chuo to compile thirty-six articles into five scrolls and promulgate them throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 其後以河南趙肅為廷尉卿，撰定法律。

translations.literal: Afterward Zhao Su of Henan was made Commandant of Justice to compile and fix the law.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Su of Henan was then appointed Commandant of Justice to codify the law.

sentences.zh: 肅積思累年，遂感心疾而死。

translations.literal: Su accumulated thought over many years and finally died of heart disease.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Su worked for many years and finally died of heart disease.

sentences.zh: 乃命司憲大夫託拔迪掌之。

translations.literal: He then ordered Grand Master of Censors Tuoba Di to take charge of it.
translations.idiomatic: Tuoba Di, Grand Master of Censors, was then charged with the task.

sentences.zh: 至保定三年三月庚子乃就，謂之大律，凡二十五篇：一曰刑名，二曰法例，三曰祀享，四曰朝會，五曰婚姻，六曰戶禁，七曰水火，八曰興繕，九曰衞宮，十曰市廛，十一曰鬬競，十二曰劫盜，十三曰賊叛，十四曰毀亡，十五曰違制，十六曰關津，十七曰諸侯，十八曰廐牧，十九曰雜犯，二十曰詐偽，二十一曰請求，二十二曰告言，二十三曰逃亡，二十四曰繫訊，二十五曰斷獄。

translations.literal: In the third year of Baoding, third month, day gengzi, it was completed, called the Great Code, twenty-five chapters in all: first, Names of Punishments; second, Legal Precedents; third, Sacrifices; fourth, Court Audiences; fifth, Marriage; sixth, Household Prohibitions; seventh, Fire and Water; eighth, Construction; ninth, Palace Guard; tenth, Markets; eleventh, Fighting; twelfth, Robbery and Plunder; thirteenth, Rebellion and Treason; fourteenth, Destruction and Loss; fifteenth, Violating Regulations; sixteenth, Passes and Tolls; seventeenth, Feudal Lords; eighteenth, Stables and Herds; nineteenth, Miscellaneous Offenses; twentieth, Fraud and Forgery; twenty-first, Requests; twenty-second, Accusation; twenty-third, Flight; twenty-fourth, Detention and Interrogation; twenty-fifth, Trial and Judgment.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoding 3, third month, day gengzi, it was completed as the Great Code in twenty-five chapters: Names of Punishments, Legal Precedents, Sacrifices, Court Audiences, Marriage, Household Prohibitions, Fire and Water, Construction, Palace Guard, Markets, Fighting, Robbery and Plunder, Rebellion and Treason, Destruction and Loss, Violating Regulations, Passes and Tolls, Feudal Lords, Stables and Herds, Miscellaneous Offenses, Fraud and Forgery, Requests, Accusation, Flight, Detention and Interrogation, and Trial and Judgment.

sentences.zh: 大凡定罪一千五百三十七條。

translations.literal: In general, fixed guilt comprised 1,537 articles.
translations.idiomatic: Criminal offenses were defined in 1,537 articles.

sentences.zh: 其制罪：一曰杖刑五，自十至五十。

translations.literal: Its fixed punishments: first, cudgel punishment, five degrees, from ten to fifty.
translations.idiomatic: Punishments were graded as follows: first, cudgel punishment in five degrees, from ten to fifty strokes.

sentences.zh: 二曰鞭刑五，自六十至于百。

translations.literal: Second, whip punishment, five degrees, from sixty to one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Second, whip punishment in five degrees, from sixty to one hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 三曰徒刑五，徒一年者，鞭六十，笞十。

translations.literal: Third, convict labor, five degrees; one year of labor, sixty strokes of whip and ten of rod.
translations.idiomatic: Third, convict labor in five degrees; one year required sixty whip strokes and ten rod strokes.

sentences.zh: 徒二年者，鞭七十，笞二十。

translations.literal: Two years of labor, seventy whip strokes and twenty rod strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Two years required seventy whip strokes and twenty rod strokes.

sentences.zh: 徒三年者，鞭八十，笞三十。

translations.literal: Three years of labor, eighty whip strokes and thirty rod strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Three years required eighty whip strokes and thirty rod strokes.

sentences.zh: 徒四年者，鞭九十，笞四十。

translations.literal: Four years of labor, ninety whip strokes and forty rod strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Four years required ninety whip strokes and forty rod strokes.

sentences.zh: 徒五年者，鞭一百，笞五十。

translations.literal: Five years of labor, one hundred whip strokes and fifty rod strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Five years required one hundred whip strokes and fifty rod strokes.

sentences.zh: 四曰流刑五，流衞服，去皇畿二千五百里者，鞭一百，笞六十。

translations.literal: Fourth, exile punishment, five degrees; exile to the guard domain, 2,500 li from the imperial domain, one hundred whip strokes and sixty rod strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, exile in five degrees; exile to the guard domain, 2,500 li from the capital, required one hundred whip strokes and sixty rod strokes.

sentences.zh: 流要服，去皇畿三千里者，鞭一百，笞七十。

translations.literal: Exile to the essential domain, 3,000 li from the imperial domain, one hundred whip strokes and seventy rod strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Exile to the essential domain, 3,000 li from the capital, required one hundred whip strokes and seventy rod strokes.

sentences.zh: 流荒服，去皇畿三千五百里者，鞭一百，笞八十。

translations.literal: Exile to the wild domain, 3,500 li, one hundred whip strokes and eighty rod strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Exile to the wild domain, 3,500 li, required one hundred whip strokes and eighty rod strokes.

sentences.zh: 流鎮服，去皇畿四千里者，鞭一百，笞九十。

translations.literal: Exile to the garrison domain, 4,000 li, one hundred whip strokes and ninety rod strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Exile to the garrison domain, 4,000 li, required one hundred whip strokes and ninety rod strokes.

sentences.zh: 流蕃服，去皇畿四千五百里者，鞭一百，笞一百。

translations.literal: Exile to the frontier domain, 4,500 li, one hundred whip strokes and one hundred rod strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Exile to the frontier domain, 4,500 li, required one hundred whip strokes and one hundred rod strokes.

sentences.zh: 五曰死刑五，一曰磬，二曰絞，三曰斬，四曰梟，五曰裂。

translations.literal: Fifth, capital punishment, five degrees: first, strangulation by cord; second, strangulation; third, decapitation; fourth, exposing the head; fifth, dismemberment.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, capital punishment in five degrees: strangulation by cord, strangulation, decapitation, exposing the head, and dismemberment.

sentences.zh: 五刑之屬各有五，合二十五等。

translations.literal: Each of the five punishments had five sub-degrees, totaling twenty-five grades.
translations.idiomatic: Each of the five punishments had five sub-degrees, totaling twenty-five grades.

sentences.zh: 不立十惡之目，而重惡逆、不道、大不敬、不孝、不義、內亂之罪。

translations.literal: They did not establish the category of ten abominations, but emphasized wicked treason, unnatural conduct, great disrespect, unfilial conduct, unrighteous conduct, and internal disorder.
translations.idiomatic: They did not establish the ten abominations as such, but emphasized wicked treason, unnatural conduct, great disrespect, unfilial conduct, unrighteous conduct, and internal disorder.

sentences.zh: 凡惡逆，肆之三日。

translations.literal: For all wicked treason, the corpse was exposed for three days.
translations.idiomatic: For wicked treason, the corpse was exposed for three days.

sentences.zh: 盜賊羣攻鄉邑及入人家者，殺之無罪。

translations.literal: Bandits and robbers who jointly attacked villages and towns and entered people's homes—killing them was not a crime.
translations.idiomatic: Killing bandits who jointly attacked villages or entered homes was not a crime.

sentences.zh: 若報讎者，告於法而自殺之，不坐。

translations.literal: If one avenged a grudge, reporting to the law and then killing oneself, there was no punishment.
translations.idiomatic: If one reported a vendetta to the authorities and then killed the offender, there was no punishment.

sentences.zh: 經為盜者，注其籍。

translations.literal: Those who had been robbers had it noted on their registers.
translations.idiomatic: Former robbers were marked on their household registers.

sentences.zh: 唯皇宗則否。

translations.literal: Only the imperial clan was exempt.
translations.idiomatic: Only the imperial clan was exempt.

sentences.zh: 凡死罪枷而拲，流罪枷而梏，徒罪枷，鞭罪桎，杖罪散以待斷。

translations.literal: Generally, capital crimes wore cangue and hand shackles; exile wore cangue and leg irons; convict labor wore cangue; whip wore leg stocks; cudgel went unrestrained pending judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Capital convicts wore cangue and hand shackles; exiles wore cangue and leg irons; convict laborers wore cangue; those subject to whip wore leg stocks; cudgel offenders went unrestrained pending judgment.

sentences.zh: 皇族及有爵者，死罪已下鎖之，徒已下散之。

translations.literal: Imperial clansmen and those with noble ranks, for capital crimes and below were chained; for convict labor and below were unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial clansmen and nobles were chained for capital crimes and below, unrestrained for convict labor and below.

sentences.zh: 獄成將殺者，書其姓名及其罪於拲，而殺之市。

translations.literal: When judgment was complete and execution imminent, their names and crimes were written on the hand shackles, and they were killed in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Before execution, names and crimes were written on the shackles, and convicts were executed in the market.

sentences.zh: 唯皇族與有爵者隱獄。

translations.literal: Only the imperial clan and those with noble ranks had hidden prisons.
translations.idiomatic: Only the imperial clan and nobles were held in private prisons.

sentences.zh: 其贖杖刑五，金一兩至五兩。

translations.literal: Ransom for five degrees of cudgel punishment: one to five liang of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Cudgel penalties could be redeemed with one to five liang of gold.

sentences.zh: 贖鞭刑五，金六兩至十兩。

translations.literal: Ransom for five degrees of whip punishment: six to ten liang of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Whip penalties could be redeemed with six to ten liang of gold.

sentences.zh: 贖徒刑五，一年金十二兩，二年十五兩，三年一斤二兩，四年一斤五兩，五年一斤八兩。

translations.literal: Ransom for five degrees of convict labor: one year twelve liang, two years fifteen liang, three years one jin two liang, four years one jin five liang, five years one jin eight liang.
translations.idiomatic: Convict labor redemption: one year twelve liang, two years fifteen liang, three years one jin two liang, four years one jin five liang, five years one jin eight liang.

sentences.zh: 贖流刑，一斤十二兩，俱役六年，不以遠近為差等。

translations.literal: Ransom for exile: one jin twelve liang, all serving six years of labor, with no difference by distance.
translations.idiomatic: Exile redemption required one jin twelve liang, with six years of labor regardless of distance.

sentences.zh: 贖死罪，金二斤。

translations.literal: Ransom for capital crimes: two jin of gold.
translations.idiomatic: Capital crimes could be redeemed with two jin of gold.

sentences.zh: 鞭者以一百為限。

translations.literal: Whipping was limited to one hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Whipping was capped at one hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 加笞者，合二百止。

translations.literal: When adding rod strokes, the total stopped at two hundred.
translations.idiomatic: When adding rod strokes, the total was capped at two hundred.

sentences.zh: 應加鞭笞者，皆先笞後鞭。

translations.literal: When whip and rod should be added, rod was applied first, then whip.
translations.idiomatic: When both rod and whip applied, rod came first, then whip.

sentences.zh: 婦人當笞者，聽以贖論。

translations.literal: Women subject to rod strokes were permitted redemption.
translations.idiomatic: Women subject to rod strokes were permitted to redeem their penalties.

sentences.zh: 徒輸作者，皆任其所能而役使之。

translations.literal: Convicts sent to labor were all assigned duties according to their abilities.
translations.idiomatic: Convict laborers were assigned duties according to their abilities.

sentences.zh: 杖十已上，當加者上就次，數滿乃坐。

translations.literal: For cudgel strokes of ten and above, when increasing, go up to the next degree; when the count was full, the sentence was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: For ten cudgel strokes and above, aggravation moved to the next degree; when the count was complete, the sentence was fixed.

sentences.zh: 當減者，死罪流蕃服，蕃服已下俱至徒五年。

translations.literal: When decreasing, capital crimes became exile to the frontier domain; below the frontier domain all reduced to five years convict labor.
translations.idiomatic: When mitigating, capital crimes became exile to the frontier domain; below that all reduced to five years convict labor.

sentences.zh: 五年以下，各以一等為差。

translations.literal: Below five years, each reduced by one degree as the difference.
translations.idiomatic: Below five years, each degree reduced by one grade.

sentences.zh: 盜賊及謀反大逆降叛惡逆罪當流者，皆甄一房配為雜戶。

translations.literal: Robbers and those guilty of rebellion, great treason, defection, and wicked treason subject to exile—all had one branch of the clan selected and assigned as miscellaneous households.
translations.idiomatic: Robbers and those guilty of rebellion, great treason, defection, or wicked treason subject to exile had one branch of the clan assigned as miscellaneous households.

sentences.zh: 其為盜賊事發逃亡者，懸名注配。

translations.literal: Those who fled after robberies occurred had their names posted and were assigned.
translations.idiomatic: Those who fled after robbery had their names posted and were assigned to penal service.

sentences.zh: 若再犯徒、三犯鞭者，一身永配下役。

translations.literal: If convict labor was committed twice or whip three times, the person was permanently assigned to menial service.
translations.idiomatic: A second convict-labor offense or third whip offense meant permanent assignment to menial service.

sentences.zh: 應贖金者，鞭杖十，收中絹一匹。

translations.literal: Those who should pay ransom gold: ten strokes of whip or cudgel collected one bolt of medium silk.
translations.idiomatic: Redemption for ten whip or cudgel strokes required one bolt of medium silk.

sentences.zh: 流徒者，依限歲收絹十二匹。

translations.literal: Exiles and convict laborers collected twelve bolts of silk per year according to the term limit.
translations.idiomatic: Exiles and convict laborers paid twelve bolts of silk per year according to their term.

sentences.zh: 死罪者一百匹。

translations.literal: Capital crimes: one hundred bolts.
translations.idiomatic: Capital crimes required one hundred bolts.

sentences.zh: 其贖刑，死罪五旬，流刑四旬，徒刑三旬，鞭刑二旬，杖刑一旬。

translations.literal: For ransom punishment: capital crimes fifty days, exile forty days, convict labor thirty days, whip twenty days, cudgel ten days.
translations.idiomatic: Redemption periods: capital fifty days, exile forty, convict labor thirty, whip twenty, cudgel ten.

sentences.zh: 限外不輸者，歸於法。

translations.literal: If not paid within the limit, judgment reverted to the law.
translations.idiomatic: Failure to pay within the deadline reverted to regular sentencing.

sentences.zh: 貧者請而免之。

translations.literal: The poor could petition and be exempted.
translations.idiomatic: The poor could petition for exemption.

sentences.zh: 大凡定法一千五百三十七條，班之天下。

translations.literal: In general the fixed law comprised 1,537 articles, promulgated throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The code comprised 1,537 articles, promulgated throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 其大略滋章，條流苛密，比於齊法，煩而不要。

translations.literal: Its general outline was increasingly detailed, articles flowing redundantly and strictly; compared with Qi law, verbose without being essential.
translations.idiomatic: Its outline grew increasingly detailed and redundant; compared with the Qi code, it was verbose without being essential.

sentences.zh: 又初除復讎之法，犯者以殺論。

translations.literal: Also at first the law of revenge was abolished; offenders were judged according to homicide.
translations.idiomatic: Private revenge was initially abolished; offenders were judged as homicides.

sentences.zh: 時晉公護將有異志，欲寬政以取人心，然闇於知人，所委多不稱職。

translations.literal: At that time Duke of Jin Hu was about to harbor rebellious intent, wishing to relax government to win people's hearts, yet he was dark in knowing men—those he entrusted were mostly unfit for their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Hu of Jin sought to relax governance to win hearts, yet poor at judging men—most of those he entrusted were unfit.

sentences.zh: 既用法寬弛，不足制姦，子弟僚屬，皆竊弄其權，百姓愁怨，控告無所。

translations.literal: Since the law was applied loosely and could not control wickedness, sons, younger brothers, and subordinates all secretly manipulated power; the common people groaned in resentment with nowhere to appeal.
translations.idiomatic: Loose enforcement failed to control crime; relatives and subordinates manipulated power while the people groaned with nowhere to appeal.

sentences.zh: 武帝性甚明察，自誅護後，躬覽萬機，雖骨肉無所縱捨，用法嚴正，中外肅然。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu was by nature very clear-sighted; after executing Hu himself, he personally attended to myriad affairs; even kin were not spared; the law was applied strictly and correctly; inside and outside were reverent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu was clear-sighted; after executing Hu he personally governed; even kin were not spared; law was strictly applied and the realm was orderly.

sentences.zh: 自魏、晉相承，死罪其重者，妻子皆以補兵。

translations.literal: Handed down from Wei and Jin, for capital crimes of the severe type, wives and children were all assigned to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Handed down from Wei and Jin, for severe capital crimes wives and children were assigned to the army.

sentences.zh: 魏虜西涼之人，沒入名為隸戶。

translations.literal: Wei captives from Western Liang were confiscated and named bond households.
translations.idiomatic: Wei captives from Western Liang were confiscated as bond households.

sentences.zh: 魏武入關，隸戶皆在東魏，後齊因之，仍供厮役。

translations.literal: When Wei Wu entered the pass, bond households were all in Eastern Wei; later Qi followed this and still supplied menial service.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Cao entered the pass, bond households remained in Eastern Wei; Northern Qi followed and kept them in menial service.

sentences.zh: 建德六年，齊平後，帝欲施輕典於新國，乃詔凡諸雜戶，悉放為百姓。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jiande, after Qi was pacified, the emperor wished to apply lenient statutes to the new state; he ordered that all miscellaneous households be released as common people.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiande 6, after pacifying Qi, the emperor ordered all miscellaneous households released as commoners.

sentences.zh: 自是無復雜戶。

translations.literal: From this there were no more miscellaneous households.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous households were abolished.

sentences.zh: 其後又以齊之舊俗，未改昏政，賊盜姦宄，頗乖憲章。

translations.literal: Afterward, because of Qi's old customs, benighted government was not reformed; bandits, robbers, treachery and villainy largely departed from statutes and regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Qi's benighted customs persisted; banditry and treachery largely ignored the code.

sentences.zh: 其年，又為刑書要制以督之。

translations.literal: That year, the Penal Essentials were also compiled to supervise this.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Penal Essentials were compiled to enforce discipline.

sentences.zh: 其大抵持仗羣盜一匹以上，不持仗羣盜五匹以上，監臨主掌自盜二十匹以上，盜及詐請官物三十匹以上，正長隱五戶及十丁以上、及地三頃以上，[10]皆死。

translations.literal: Generally, armed group robbery of one bolt and above, unarmed group robbery of five bolts and above, supervisors and managers stealing twenty bolts and above, robbery and fraudulent request of official goods thirty bolts and above, village heads concealing five households and ten adult males and above and three qing of land and above, [10] all were death.
translations.idiomatic: Armed group robbery of one bolt or more, unarmed group robbery of five bolts, supervisors stealing twenty bolts, robbery or fraud of thirty bolts of official goods, village heads concealing five households, ten adult males, or three qing of land [10]—all were capital offenses.

sentences.zh: 自餘依大律。

translations.literal: For the remainder, follow the Great Code.
translations.idiomatic: All other cases followed the Great Code.

sentences.zh: 由是澆詐頗息焉。

translations.literal: Thereby deceit and fraud largely ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Deceit and fraud largely ceased.

sentences.zh: 宣帝性殘忍暴戾，自在儲貳，惡其叔父齊王憲及王軌、宇文孝伯等。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan was by nature cruel, violent, and tyrannical; while still heir apparent, he hated his uncle Prince Qi of Qi, Wang Gui, Yuwen Xiaobo, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan was cruel and tyrannical; as heir he hated his uncle Prince Qi, Wang Gui, Yuwen Xiaobo, and others.

sentences.zh: 及即位，並先誅戮，由是內外不安，俱懷危懼。

translations.literal: Upon ascending the throne, all were first executed; thereby inside and outside were unsettled, all harboring fear and dread.
translations.idiomatic: Upon taking the throne he executed them all; fear spread throughout the court.

sentences.zh: 帝又恐失眾望，乃行寬法，以取眾心。

translations.literal: The emperor also feared losing public support, and therefore applied lenient law to win people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing loss of public support, he applied lenient law to win hearts.

sentences.zh: 宣政元年八月，詔制九條，宣下州郡。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Xuanzheng, a nine-article code was promulgated to prefectures and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Xuanzheng 1, a nine-article code was promulgated to prefectures and commanderies.

sentences.zh: 大象元年，又下詔曰：「高祖所立刑書要制，用法深重，其一切除之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daxiang, another edict said: "The Penal Essentials established by the High Ancestor applied the law with heavy severity—all are completely abolished."
translations.idiomatic: In Daxiang 1, another edict abolished the Penal Essentials established by the High Ancestor as too severe.

sentences.zh: 」然帝荒淫日甚，惡聞其過，誅殺無度，疎斥大臣。

translations.literal: Yet the emperor's debauchery grew daily worse; he hated to hear of his faults; executions were limitless; great ministers were cast aside.
translations.idiomatic: Yet debauchery grew daily; he hated criticism; executions were limitless; great ministers were cast aside.

sentences.zh: 又數行肆赦，為姦者皆輕犯刑法，政令不一，下無適從。

translations.literal: Also repeatedly granting universal amnesty, wicked persons all lightly violated the penal law; government orders were not unified; below there was nothing to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated amnesties let criminals lightly violate the law; government orders lacked unity and none knew what to follow.

sentences.zh: 於是又廣刑書要制，而更峻其法，謂之刑經聖制。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Penal Essentials were again expanded and the law made more severe, called the Penal Canon of Sage Governance.
translations.idiomatic: The Penal Essentials were expanded and the law made harsher, styled the Penal Canon of Sage Governance.

sentences.zh: 宿衞之官，一日不直，罪至削除。

translations.literal: Palace guard officials who failed to stand duty one day were punished by removal from office.
translations.idiomatic: Palace guards who missed one day of duty were removed from office.

sentences.zh: 逃亡者皆死，而家口籍沒。

translations.literal: Fugitives were all executed, and household members' registers confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Fugitives were executed and their households' registers confiscated.

sentences.zh: 上書字誤者，科其罪。

translations.literal: Those who made errors in characters when submitting memorials were punished for the offense.
translations.idiomatic: Memorials with character errors incurred punishment.

sentences.zh: 鞭杖皆百二十為度，名曰天杖。

translations.literal: Whip and cudgel were all one hundred twenty as the measure, called the Heavenly Cudgel.
translations.idiomatic: Whip and cudgel were capped at one hundred twenty strokes, called the Heavenly Cudgel.

sentences.zh: 其後又加至二百四十。

translations.literal: Later it was again increased to two hundred forty.
translations.idiomatic: Later the limit was raised to two hundred forty.

sentences.zh: 又作礔礰車，以威婦人。

translations.literal: Also made was the crushing cart to intimidate women.
translations.idiomatic: A crushing cart was also devised to intimidate women.

sentences.zh: 其決人罪，云與杖者，即一百二十，多打者，即二百四十。

translations.literal: When deciding people's crimes, if it said 'give cudgel,' then one hundred twenty; if more beating, then two hundred forty.
translations.idiomatic: Sentences specifying cudgel meant one hundred twenty strokes; heavier beating meant two hundred forty.

sentences.zh: 帝既酣飲過度，嘗中飲，有下士楊文祐白宮伯長孫覽，求歌曰：「朝亦醉，暮亦醉。

translations.literal: The emperor being given to excessive drinking, once while drunk, lower officer Yang Wenyou told Palace Steward Chief Sun Lan, requesting a song saying: "Drunk in the morning, drunk in the evening.
translations.idiomatic: Given to excessive drinking, once while drunk lower officer Yang Wenyou asked Palace Steward Chief Sun Lan for a song: "Drunk in the morning, drunk in the evening.

sentences.zh: 日日恒常醉，政事日無次。

translations.literal: Daily constantly drunk, government affairs daily without order.
translations.idiomatic: Daily drunk, government affairs daily in disorder."

sentences.zh: 」鄭譯奏之，帝怒，命賜杖二百四十而致死。

translations.literal: Zheng Yi memorialized this; the emperor was angry and ordered two hundred forty strokes of cudgel given until death.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yi reported this; the emperor ordered two hundred forty strokes until death.

sentences.zh: 後更令中士皇甫猛歌，猛歌又諷諫。

translations.literal: Later he again ordered middle officer Huangfu Meng to sing; Meng's song again remonstrated and admonished.
translations.idiomatic: He later ordered middle officer Huangfu Meng to sing; Meng's song again remonstrated.

sentences.zh: 鄭譯又以奏之，又賜猛杖一百二十。

translations.literal: Zheng Yi again memorialized this; he again gave Meng one hundred twenty strokes of cudgel.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yi reported this again; Meng received one hundred twenty strokes.

sentences.zh: 是時下自公卿，內及妃后，咸加棰楚，上下愁怨。

translations.literal: At that time from dukes and ministers down, and consorts and empresses within, all received beating and cudgeling; above and below groaned in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: From dukes and ministers to consorts and empresses, all received beatings; resentment spread above and below.

sentences.zh: 及帝不豫，而內外離心，各求苟免。

translations.literal: When the emperor fell ill, inside and outside lost heart, each seeking mere escape.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill, the court lost heart and all sought merely to survive.

sentences.zh: 隋高祖為相，又行寬大之典，刪略舊律，作刑書要制。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu of Sui was Chancellor, he again applied lenient statutes, abridged the old code, and made the Penal Essentials.
translations.idiomatic: As Chancellor, Emperor Wen of Sui applied lenient statutes, abridged the old code, and compiled the Penal Essentials.

sentences.zh: 既成奏之，靜帝下詔頒行。

translations.literal: When completed and submitted, Emperor Jing issued an edict promulgating it.
translations.idiomatic: When completed, Emperor Jing promulgated it by edict.

sentences.zh: 諸有犯罪未科決者，並依制處斷。

translations.literal: All who had committed offenses not yet judged were all decided according to the code.
translations.idiomatic: All pending cases were decided according to the new code.

sentences.zh: 高祖既受周禪，開皇元年，乃詔尚書左僕射、勃海公高熲，上柱國、沛公鄭譯，上柱國、清河郡公楊素，大理前少卿、平源縣公常明，刑部侍郎、保城縣公韓濬，比部侍郎李諤，兼考功侍郎柳雄亮等，更定新律，奏上之。

translations.literal: After Gaozu received the Zhou abdication, in the first year of Kaihuang, he ordered Left Vice Minister of Justice Gao Jiong of Bohai, Upper Pillar of State Zheng Yi of Pei, Upper Pillar of State Yang Su of Qinghe, former Vice Director of the Court of Justice Chang Ming of Pingyuan, Vice Director of the Punishments Section Han Jun of Baocheng, Vice Director of the Comparison Section Li E, and Concurrent Vice Director of the Merit Section Liu Xiongliang and others to further fix the new code and submit it.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaihuang 1, after receiving the Zhou abdication, he ordered Gao Jiong, Zheng Yi, Yang Su, Chang Ming, Han Jun, Li E, Liu Xiongliang, and others to revise the new code.

sentences.zh: 其刑名有五：一曰死刑二，有絞，有斬。

translations.literal: Its punishment names were five: first, capital punishment, two kinds—strangulation and decapitation.
translations.idiomatic: Five categories of punishment were established: first, capital punishment in two forms—strangulation and decapitation.

sentences.zh: 二曰流刑三，有一千里、千五百里、二千里。

translations.literal: Second, exile punishment, three kinds—one thousand li, one thousand five hundred li, two thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Second, exile in three degrees—one thousand, one thousand five hundred, and two thousand li.

sentences.zh: 應配者，一千里居作二年，一千五百里居作二年半，二千里居作三年。

translations.literal: Those who should be assigned: one thousand li, two years labor; one thousand five hundred li, two and a half years; two thousand li, three years.
translations.idiomatic: Assignment terms: one thousand li, two years labor; one thousand five hundred li, two and a half years; two thousand li, three years.

sentences.zh: 應住居作者，三流俱役三年。

translations.literal: Those who should remain and do labor, all three exiles served three years.
translations.idiomatic: Those remaining to serve labor: all three exile degrees required three years.

sentences.zh: 近流加杖一百，一等加三十。

translations.literal: Near exile added one hundred strokes of cudgel; each degree added thirty.
translations.idiomatic: The nearest exile added one hundred cudgel strokes; each degree added thirty.

sentences.zh: 三曰徒刑五，有一年、一年半、二年、二年半、三年。

translations.literal: Third, convict labor, five kinds—one year, one and a half years, two years, two and a half years, three years.
translations.idiomatic: Third, convict labor in five terms—one, one and a half, two, two and a half, and three years.

sentences.zh: 四曰杖刑五，自五十至于百。

translations.literal: Fourth, cudgel punishment, five kinds—from fifty to one hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, cudgel punishment from fifty to one hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 五曰笞刑五，自十至于五十。

translations.literal: Fifth, rod punishment, five kinds—from ten to fifty.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, rod punishment from ten to fifty strokes.

sentences.zh: 而蠲除前代鞭刑及梟首轘裂之法。

translations.literal: And abolished the whip punishment of former generations and the methods of exposing the head, dismemberment at the waist, and tearing apart.
translations.idiomatic: Whip punishment and the methods of exposing the head, dismemberment, and tearing apart were abolished.

sentences.zh: 其流徒之罪皆減從輕。

translations.literal: Exile and convict labor crimes were all reduced and followed the lighter.
translations.idiomatic: Exile and convict labor penalties were all reduced toward leniency.

sentences.zh: [11]唯大逆謀反叛者，父子兄弟皆斬，家口沒官。

translations.literal: [11] Only for great treason and plotting rebellion, fathers, sons, and brothers were all beheaded, household members confiscated by the state.
translations.idiomatic: [11] Only for great treason and plotting rebellion were fathers, sons, and brothers beheaded and household members confiscated.

sentences.zh: 又置十惡之條，多採後齊之制，而頗有損益。

translations.literal: Also established the ten abominations, largely drawn from later Qi's system, yet with additions and reductions.
translations.idiomatic: The ten abominations were established, largely drawn from Northern Qi with modifications.

sentences.zh: 一曰謀反，二曰謀大逆，三曰謀叛，四曰惡逆，五曰不道，六曰大不敬，七曰不孝，八曰不睦，九曰不義，十曰內亂。

translations.literal: First, plotting rebellion; second, plotting great treason; third, plotting defection; fourth, wicked treason; fifth, unnatural conduct; sixth, great disrespect; seventh, unfilial conduct; eighth, discord within the clan; ninth, unrighteous conduct; tenth, internal disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The ten abominations: plotting rebellion, plotting great treason, plotting defection, wicked treason, unnatural conduct, great disrespect, unfilial conduct, discord within the clan, unrighteous conduct, and internal disorder.

sentences.zh: 犯十惡及故殺人獄成者，雖會赦，猶除名。

translations.literal: Those who committed the ten abominations and intentional homicide with judgment complete, even if amnesty occurred, were still removed from registers.
translations.idiomatic: Those guilty of the ten abominations or intentional homicide, even under amnesty, were removed from registers.

sentences.zh: 其在八議之科，及官品第七已上犯罪，皆例減一等。

translations.literal: Those in the eight deliberations and officials of rank seven and above who committed crimes—all by precedent reduced one degree.
translations.idiomatic: Those in the eight deliberations and officials of rank seven and above received one degree of reduction.

sentences.zh: 其品第九已上犯者，聽贖。

translations.literal: Those of rank nine and above who committed crimes were permitted ransom.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of rank nine and above were permitted redemption.

sentences.zh: 應贖者，皆以銅代絹。

translations.literal: Those who should ransom all used copper in place of silk.
translations.idiomatic: Redemption was paid in copper rather than silk.

sentences.zh: 贖銅一斤為一負，負十為殿。

translations.literal: Ransom copper one jin equaled one demerit; ten demerits equaled one dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: One jin of copper equaled one demerit; ten demerits equaled dismissal.

sentences.zh: 笞十者銅一斤，加至杖百則十斤。

translations.literal: Ten rod strokes, one jin of copper; increasing to one hundred cudgel strokes then ten jin.
translations.idiomatic: Ten rod strokes required one jin of copper; one hundred cudgel strokes required ten jin.

sentences.zh: 徒一年，贖銅二十斤，每等則加銅十斤，三年則六十斤矣。

translations.literal: One year convict labor, twenty jin of ransom copper; each degree added ten jin of copper; three years then sixty jin.
translations.idiomatic: One year of convict labor required twenty jin of copper; each degree added ten jin, three years sixty jin.

sentences.zh: 流一千里，贖銅八十斤，每等則加銅十斤，二千里則百斤矣。

translations.literal: Exile one thousand li, eighty jin of ransom copper; each degree added ten jin; two thousand li then one hundred jin.
translations.idiomatic: Exile one thousand li required eighty jin; each degree added ten jin, two thousand li one hundred jin.

sentences.zh: 二死皆贖銅百二十斤。

translations.literal: Both capital punishments ransom one hundred twenty jin of copper.
translations.idiomatic: Both forms of capital punishment required one hundred twenty jin of copper for redemption.

sentences.zh: 犯私罪以官當徒者，五品已上，一官當徒二年；

translations.literal: When private offenses used office to commute convict labor: rank five and above, one office post commuted two years;
translations.idiomatic: For private offenses, rank five and above could commute two years of convict labor per office held;

sentences.zh: 九品已上，一官當徒一年；

translations.literal: rank nine and above, one office post commuted one year;
translations.idiomatic: rank nine and above, one year per office held;

sentences.zh: 當流者。

translations.literal: when commuting exile.
translations.idiomatic: when commuting exile.

sentences.zh: 三流同比徒三年。

translations.literal: All three exiles compared equally to three years convict labor.
translations.idiomatic: All three exile degrees equaled three years of convict labor.

sentences.zh: [12]若犯公罪者，徒各加一年，當流者各加一等。

translations.literal: [12] If public offenses, convict labor each added one year; exile each added one degree.
translations.idiomatic: [12] For public offenses, convict labor added one year; exile added one degree.

sentences.zh: 其累徒過九年者，流二千里。

translations.literal: If accumulated convict labor exceeded nine years, exile two thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Accumulated convict labor exceeding nine years became exile two thousand li.

sentences.zh: 定訖，詔頒之曰：「帝王作法，沿革不同，取適於時，故有損益。

translations.literal: When fixed, an edict promulgated it saying: "Emperors and kings make law; following and changing differ; taking what suits the times, therefore there are additions and reductions.
translations.idiomatic: When finalized, an edict declared: "Emperors make law that changes with the times; therefore there are additions and reductions.

sentences.zh: 夫絞以致斃，斬則殊刑，除惡之體，於斯已極。

translations.literal: Strangulation to cause death, decapitation then separate punishment—the substance of eliminating evil, in this already extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Strangulation and decapitation already represent the utmost in eliminating evil.

sentences.zh: 梟首轘身，義無所取，不益懲肅之理，徒表安忍之懷。

translations.literal: Exposing the head and dismembering the body—in meaning nothing to take; not increasing the principle of punishing and revering, merely showing a disposition of cruel endurance.
translations.idiomatic: Exposing the head and dismembering the body serve no purpose; they do not increase deterrence, only display cruelty.

sentences.zh: 鞭之為用，殘剝膚體，徹骨侵肌，酷均臠切。

translations.literal: The use of the whip mutilates and strips flesh and skin, penetrating bone and invading muscle—cruelty equal to carving and cutting.
translations.idiomatic: The whip mutilates flesh and penetrates bone—cruelty equal to carving and cutting.

sentences.zh: 雖云遠古之式，事乖仁者之刑，梟轘及鞭，並令去也。

translations.literal: Although called an ancient form, the matter departs from the punishment of the benevolent; exposing the head, dismemberment, and whip—all are ordered removed.
translations.idiomatic: Though called ancient forms, they depart from benevolent punishment; exposing the head, dismemberment, and the whip are all abolished.

sentences.zh: 貴礪帶之書，不當徒罰，廣軒冕之蔭，旁及諸親。

translations.literal: Valuing the book of polished girdle-pendants, convict labor punishment is not appropriate; broadly extending the shade of carriage-canopies and caps, extending to all kin.
translations.idiomatic: Honored officials should not receive convict labor; noble rank extends protection to kin.

sentences.zh: 流役六年，改為五載，刑徒五歲，變從三祀。

translations.literal: Exile service six years changed to five; convict labor five years changed to three.
translations.idiomatic: Exile service was reduced from six years to five; convict labor from five years to three.

sentences.zh: 其餘以輕代重，化死為生，條目甚多，備於簡策。

translations.literal: For the remainder, using light in place of heavy, transforming death into life—the articles are many, complete in the brief scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Elsewhere light replaced heavy and death became life—the articles are many, recorded in full.

sentences.zh: 宜班諸海內，為時軌範，雜格嚴科，並宜除削。

translations.literal: It should be promulgated throughout the realm as the standard of the times; miscellaneous codes and strict categories should all be abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Let it be promulgated throughout the realm as the standard of the age; miscellaneous codes and harsh categories are abolished.

sentences.zh: 先施法令，欲人無犯之心，國有常刑，誅而不怒之義。

translations.literal: First applying statutes and ordinances is to make people have no mind to transgress; the state has regular punishment—the meaning of executing without anger.
translations.idiomatic: Law is applied so people will not transgress; regular punishment means executing without anger.

sentences.zh: 措而不用，庶或非遠，萬方百辟，知吾此懷。

translations.literal: Setting aside and not using it—perhaps not far off; the myriad regions and hundred officials, know our intent.
translations.idiomatic: Setting punishment aside may not be far off; let all officials know our intent."

sentences.zh: 」自前代相承，有司訊考，皆以法外。

translations.literal: Handed down from former generations, when relevant offices interrogated and examined, all were outside the law.
translations.idiomatic: Handed down from former dynasties, interrogation often went outside the law.

sentences.zh: 或有用大棒束杖，車輻鞵底，壓踝杖桄之屬，楚毒備至，多所誣伏。

translations.literal: Some used great cudgels, bound cudgels, wagon-spoke cudgels, sole-beating, ankle-pressing, and cudgel-yoke and the like; torture complete, much leading to false confession.
translations.idiomatic: Some used great cudgels, wagon spokes, sole-beating, ankle-pressing, and cudgel-yokes; torture produced many false confessions.

sentences.zh: 雖文致於法，而每有枉濫，莫能自理。

translations.literal: Although the text led to the law, yet often there was wrongful conviction; none could justify themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Though cases conformed to the letter of the law, wrongful convictions were common and none could defend themselves.

sentences.zh: 至是盡除苛慘之法，訊囚不得過二百，枷杖大小，咸為之程品，行杖者不得易人。

translations.literal: By this all harsh and cruel methods were completely abolished; interrogating prisoners could not exceed two hundred strokes; cangue and cudgel, large and small, all had regulated grades; those applying cudgel could not change persons.
translations.idiomatic: All harsh methods were abolished; interrogation was capped at two hundred strokes; cangue and cudgel sizes were standardized; beaters could not be changed.

sentences.zh: 帝又以律令初行，人未知禁，故犯法者眾。

translations.literal: The emperor also thought that when statutes and ordinances first ran, people did not yet know prohibitions; therefore offenders were many.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also recognized that when the new code first took effect, many violated it through ignorance.

sentences.zh: 又下吏承苛政之後，務鍛鍊以致人罪。

translations.literal: Also lower officials, inheriting harsh government afterward, strove to forge and refine to bring people to guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Lower officials, inheriting harsh practices, strove to forge cases against the accused.

sentences.zh: 乃詔申勑四方，敦理辭訟。

translations.literal: He then ordered proclamation to the four directions, earnestly settling lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered proclamation throughout the realm to earnestly settle lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 有枉屈縣不理者，令以次經郡及州，至省仍不理，[13]乃詣闕申訴。

translations.literal: If there was wrongful conviction that the county did not settle, order proceeding in order through the commandery and prefecture, to the province; if still not settled, [13] then go to the palace to appeal.
translations.idiomatic: Wrongful convictions unsettled at county level proceeded through commandery and prefecture to province; if still unsettled, [13] appeal went to the palace.

sentences.zh: 有所未愜，聽撾登聞鼓，有司錄狀奏之。

translations.literal: If something was not satisfactory, permitted beating the petition drum; relevant offices recorded the petition and memorialized it.
translations.idiomatic: If unsatisfied, petitioners could beat the petition drum; officials recorded and memorialized the case.

sentences.zh: 帝又每季親錄囚徒。

translations.literal: The emperor also each season personally reviewed prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also personally reviewed prisoners each season.

sentences.zh: 常以秋分之前，省閱諸州申奏罪狀。

translations.literal: Regularly before the autumn equinox, reviewed crime reports submitted by all prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Regularly before the autumn equinox he reviewed crime reports from all prefectures.

sentences.zh: 三年，因覽刑部奏，斷獄數猶至萬條。

translations.literal: In the third year, while reviewing the Punishments Section memorial, cases judged still reached ten thousand entries.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, reviewing the Punishments Section memorial, judged cases still reached ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 以為律尚嚴密，故人多陷罪。

translations.literal: He thought the code was still strict and dense; therefore many people fell into guilt.
translations.idiomatic: He concluded the code was still too strict, trapping many in guilt.

sentences.zh: 又勑蘇威、牛弘等，更定新律。

translations.literal: Also ordered Su Wei, Niu Hong, and others to further fix the new code.
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei, Niu Hong, and others were ordered to revise the code further.

sentences.zh: 除死罪八十一條，流罪一百五十四條，徒杖等千餘條，定留唯五百條。

translations.literal: Abolished eighty-one capital articles, one hundred fifty-four exile articles, over one thousand convict labor and cudgel articles; fixed retention was only five hundred articles.
translations.idiomatic: Eighty-one capital articles, one hundred fifty-four exile articles, and over one thousand convict-labor and cudgel articles were cut; only five hundred remained.

sentences.zh: 凡十二卷。

translations.literal: Twelve scrolls in all.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve scrolls in all.

sentences.zh: 一曰名例，二曰衞禁，三曰職制，四曰戶婚，五曰廐庫，六曰擅興，七曰賊盜，八曰鬬訟，九曰詐偽，十曰雜律，十一曰捕亡，十二曰斷獄。

translations.literal: First, Names and Examples; second, Forbidden Guard; third, Office System; fourth, Households and Marriage; fifth, Stables and Granaries; sixth, Unauthorized Mobilization; seventh, Bandits and Robbers; eighth, Fighting and Litigation; ninth, Fraud and Forgery; tenth, Miscellaneous Statutes; eleventh, Pursuit of Fugitives; twelfth, Trial and Judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Twelve chapters: Names and Examples, Forbidden Guard, Office System, Households and Marriage, Stables and Granaries, Unauthorized Mobilization, Bandits and Robbers, Fighting and Litigation, Fraud and Forgery, Miscellaneous Statutes, Pursuit of Fugitives, and Trial and Judgment.

sentences.zh: 自是刑網簡要，疎而不失。

translations.literal: From this the penal net was concise and brief, sparse yet without loss.
translations.idiomatic: The penal net became concise—sparse yet without loss.

sentences.zh: 於是置律博士弟子員。

translations.literal: Thereupon Doctor of Law disciples were established.
translations.idiomatic: Doctor of Law disciples were established.

sentences.zh: 斷決大獄，皆先牒明法，定其罪名，然後依斷。

translations.literal: Deciding great cases all first submitted to the legal expert to fix the charge name, then judged according to it.
translations.idiomatic: Major cases first went to legal experts to fix the charge, then judgment followed.

sentences.zh: 五年，侍官慕容天遠，糾都督田元，冒請義倉，事實而始平縣律生輔恩，舞文陷天遠，遂更反坐。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Attendant Official Murong Tianyuan impeached Supervisor Tian Yuan for falsely requesting charity grain; the facts were true, yet Pingyuan County legal student Fu En twisted the text to trap Tianyuan, and the charge was reversed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year, Murong Tianyuan impeached Supervisor Tian Yuan for falsely requesting charity grain; the facts were true, yet legal student Fu En twisted the text to trap Tianyuan, reversing the charge.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，乃下詔曰：「人命之重，懸在律文，刊定科條，俾令易曉。

translations.literal: The emperor heard this and issued an edict saying: "Human life is heavy, suspended on the text of the code; fixing and determining articles and categories should make them easy to understand.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict: "Human life depends on the code; articles must be easy to understand.

sentences.zh: 分官命職，恒選循吏，小大之獄，理無疑舛。

translations.literal: Assigning offices and appointing duties, constantly selecting upright officials—great and small cases, in principle without doubt or error.
translations.idiomatic: Appoint upright officials so great and small cases are decided without error.

sentences.zh: 而因襲往代，別置律官，報判之人，推其為首。

translations.literal: Yet following former generations, separately establishing legal officials—those reporting judgment pushed them as leaders.
translations.idiomatic: Yet following former practice, separate legal officials were established and treated as leaders in judgment.

sentences.zh: 殺生之柄，常委小人，刑罰所以未清，威褔所以妄作。

translations.literal: The power of taking life was constantly entrusted to petty men; punishment therefore was not clear, authority and blessing therefore was wantonly exercised.
translations.idiomatic: The power of life and death was entrusted to petty men; punishment was unclear and authority was wantonly exercised.

sentences.zh: 為政之失，莫大於斯。

translations.literal: In governing, no failure is greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: No failure in governance is greater than this.

sentences.zh: 其大理律博士、尚書刑部曹明法、州縣律生，並可停廢。

translations.literal: The Court of Justice Doctor of Law, Ministry of Justice Punishments Section legal expert, and prefectural and county legal students—all may be stopped and abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Court of Justice Doctors of Law, Ministry legal experts, and prefectural legal students are all abolished."

sentences.zh: 」自是諸曹決事，皆令具寫律文斷之。

translations.literal: From this all bureaus deciding matters were all ordered to fully write out the text of the code in deciding.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter all bureaus were ordered to cite the code text fully in their decisions.

sentences.zh: 六年，勑諸州長史已下，行參軍已上，並令習律，集京之日，試其通不。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, ordered all prefectural chief administrators and below, military adjutants and above, all to study the code; on arriving at the capital, test their mastery.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year, all prefectural administrators and military adjutants were ordered to study the code and be tested on reaching the capital.

sentences.zh: 又詔免尉迥、王謙、司馬消難三道逆人家口之配沒者，悉官酬贖，使為編戶。

translations.literal: Also ordered that household members confiscated from the three rebellious lines of Yuchi Jiong, Wang Qian, and Sima Xiaonan be officially ransomed and released as registered households.
translations.idiomatic: Households confiscated from the rebellions of Yuchi Jiong, Wang Qian, and Sima Xiaonan were ransomed and restored as registered households.

sentences.zh: 因除孥戮相坐之法。

translations.literal: Thereby the law of punishing the family and joint punishment was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Family punishment and joint liability were thereby abolished.

sentences.zh: 又命諸州囚有處死，不得馳驛行決。

translations.literal: Also ordered that in all prefectures, prisoners facing execution could not be executed by express relay.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures were forbidden to execute prisoners by express relay.

sentences.zh: 高祖性猜忌，素不悅學，既任智而獲大位，因以文法自矜，明察臨下。

translations.literal: Gaozu was by nature suspicious and jealous, never pleased with learning; having relied on intelligence to obtain the great position, he therefore prided himself on legal text, clear-sighted in overseeing subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen was suspicious and disliked learning; having risen through wit, he prided himself on legal knowledge and watched subordinates keenly.

sentences.zh: 恒令左右覘視內外，有小過失，則加以重罪。

translations.literal: Constantly ordered those around him to observe inside and outside; for small faults, heavy punishment was added.
translations.idiomatic: He constantly ordered attendants to spy inside and outside; small faults brought heavy punishment.

sentences.zh: 又患令史贓汚，因私使人以錢帛遺之，得犯立斬。

translations.literal: Also worrying that clerks were corrupt, he privately sent people with money and silk to bribe them; if they violated, immediate execution.
translations.idiomatic: Suspecting clerical corruption, he secretly sent bribes; violators were immediately executed.

sentences.zh: 每於殿廷打人，一日之中，或至數四。

translations.literal: Each day in the palace hall he beat people; in one day sometimes up to three or four times.
translations.idiomatic: He beat people daily in the palace hall, sometimes three or four times in one day.

sentences.zh: 嘗怒問事揮楚不甚，即命斬之。

translations.literal: Once angry at an interrogator's beating not being severe enough, he immediately ordered execution.
translations.idiomatic: Once angry that an interrogator's beating was too light, he ordered immediate execution.

sentences.zh: 十年，尚書左僕射高熲、治書侍御史柳彧等諫，以為朝堂非殺人之所，殿庭非決罰之地。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, Left Vice Minister Gao Jiong, Imperial Censor Liu Yu, and others remonstrated, thinking the court hall was not a place for killing people, the palace hall not a place for deciding punishment.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, Gao Jiong, Liu Yu, and others remonstrated that the court hall was no place for killing, the palace no place for punishment.

sentences.zh: 帝不納。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor did not accept their advice.

sentences.zh: 熲等乃盡詣朝堂請罪，曰：「陛下子育羣生，務在去弊，而百姓無知，犯者不息，致陛下決罰過嚴。

translations.literal: Jiong and others then all went to the court hall requesting punishment, saying: "Your Majesty nurtures and raises the multitude; striving to remove abuses; yet the common people, not knowing, offenders do not cease, causing Your Majesty's decisions and punishments to be excessively strict.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong and others then requested punishment at court: "Your Majesty nurtures the people and seeks to remove abuses, yet offenders persist, forcing excessively strict punishment.

sentences.zh: 皆臣等不能有所裨益，請自退屏，以避賢路。

translations.literal: All we ministers cannot offer benefit; please ourselves withdraw and yield the path of the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: We ministers have failed; we beg to withdraw and yield to worthier men."

sentences.zh: 」帝於是顧謂領左右都督田元曰：「吾杖重乎？

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon looked at Chief of Attendants Tian Yuan and said: "Are my beatings heavy?
