translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned to Chief of Attendants Tian Yuan: "Are my beatings too heavy?"

sentences.zh: 」元曰：「重。

translations.literal: Yuan said: "Heavy."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan replied: "Heavy."

sentences.zh: 」帝問其狀，元舉手曰：「陛下杖大如指，棰楚人三十者，比常杖數百，故多致死。

translations.literal: The emperor asked the details; Yuan raised his hand saying: "Your Majesty's cudgel is as large as a finger; beating people thirty times compares to several hundred ordinary cudgel strokes, therefore many die."
translations.idiomatic: Yuan raised his hand: "Your Majesty's rod is thick as a finger; thirty strokes compare to several hundred ordinary strokes, so many die."

sentences.zh: 」帝不懌，乃令殿內去杖，欲有決罰，各付所由。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and ordered cudgels removed from within the hall; when punishment was to be decided, each was assigned to the relevant office.
translations.idiomatic: Displeased, the emperor removed cudgels from the hall; punishments were assigned to the relevant offices.

sentences.zh: 後楚州行參軍李君才上言，帝寵高熲過甚，上大怒，命杖之，而殿內無杖，遂以馬鞭笞殺之。

translations.literal: Later Chuzhou Military Adjutant Li Juncai submitted a memorial saying the emperor favored Gao Jiong excessively; the emperor was greatly angry and ordered beating; yet within the hall there was no cudgel, so he was flogged to death with a horsewhip.
translations.idiomatic: Later Li Juncai submitted that the emperor favored Gao Jiong excessively; enraged, the emperor ordered a beating; with no cudgel in the hall, Li was flogged to death with a horsewhip.

sentences.zh: 自是殿內復置杖。

translations.literal: From this cudgels were again placed within the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Cudgels were restored to the hall.

sentences.zh: 未幾怒甚，又於殿庭殺人，兵部侍郎馮基固諫，帝不從，竟於殿庭行決。

translations.literal: Before long, greatly angry again, he again killed people in the palace hall; Vice Director of the Ministry of War Feng Ji firmly remonstrated; the emperor did not follow; ultimately execution was carried out in the palace hall.
translations.idiomatic: Soon angry again, he killed in the hall; Feng Ji remonstrated in vain; execution proceeded in the hall.

sentences.zh: 帝亦尋悔，宣慰馮基，而怒羣僚之不諫者。

translations.literal: The emperor also soon regretted it, sent consolation to Feng Ji, yet was angry that the multitude of officials did not remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: He soon regretted it and consoled Feng Ji, yet was angry that other officials had not remonstrated.

sentences.zh: 十二年，帝以用律者多致踳駁，罪同論異。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, the emperor thought that in applying the code many led to contradiction and rejection; crimes were the same yet deliberation differed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, the emperor found that applying the code produced contradictions—identical crimes judged differently.

sentences.zh: 詔諸州死罪不得便決，悉移大理案覆，事盡然後上省奏裁。

translations.literal: He ordered that in all prefectures capital crimes could not be immediately decided; all were transferred to the Court of Justice for case review; when matters were complete, then submitted to the province for memorial and decision.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectures were forbidden to decide capital cases immediately; all went to the Court of Justice for review, then to the province for final decision.

sentences.zh: 十三年，改徒及流並為配防。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, convict labor and exile were both changed to frontier assignment.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, convict labor and exile were both changed to frontier assignment.

sentences.zh: 十五年制，死罪者三奏而後決。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year system, capital crimes required three submissions before execution.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year, capital crimes required three reviews before execution.

sentences.zh: 十六年，有司奏合川倉粟少七千石，命斛律孝卿鞫問其事，以為主典所竊。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, the relevant offices memorialized that Hechuan granary grain was short seven thousand shi; he ordered Hulu Xiaoqing to interrogate the matter, thinking the chief clerk had stolen it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, officials reported Hechuan granary short seven thousand shi; Hulu Xiaoqing was ordered to investigate, blaming the chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 復令孝卿馳驛斬之，沒其家為奴婢，鬻粟以填之。

translations.literal: Again ordered Xiaoqing by express relay to execute; his household was confiscated as slave servants; the grain was sold to fill the deficit.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoqing was ordered by express relay to execute him; his household was enslaved; grain was sold to cover the deficit.

sentences.zh: 是後盜邊糧者，一升已上皆死，家口沒官。

translations.literal: After this, those stealing frontier grain—one sheng and above all died, household members confiscated by the state.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, stealing frontier grain of one sheng or more meant death and confiscation of household members.

sentences.zh: 上又以典吏久居其職，肆情為姦。

translations.literal: The emperor also thought that clerks long occupying their posts indulged feelings in wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also found that long-serving clerks indulged in corruption.

sentences.zh: 諸州縣佐史，三年一代，經任者不得重居之。

translations.literal: All prefectural and county assistant clerks, one generation every three years; those who had served could not again occupy the post.
translations.idiomatic: Prefectural and county clerks rotated every three years; former incumbents could not serve again.

sentences.zh: 十七年，詔又以所在官人，不相敬憚，多自寬縱，事難克舉。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, an edict also said that local officials did not respect and fear one another, mostly indulging themselves broadly; matters were hard to investigate and report.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, an edict noted that local officials indulged themselves and failed to enforce the law.

sentences.zh: 諸有殿失，雖備科條，或據律乃輕，論情則重，不即決罪，無以懲肅。

translations.literal: For all palace faults, although the code articles were complete, or according to the code it was light yet considering circumstances it was heavy—not immediately deciding guilt, there was no means to punish and reverence.
translations.idiomatic: For all offenses, though code articles existed, when the code was light yet circumstances heavy, immediate judgment could not deter wrongdoing.

sentences.zh: 其諸司屬官，若有愆犯，聽於律外斟酌決杖。

translations.literal: All subordinate officials of the various bureaus, if there were faults and violations, permitted deciding cudgel outside the code as appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Subordinate officials guilty of faults could be beaten beyond what the code prescribed.

sentences.zh: 於是上下相驅，迭行棰楚，以殘暴為幹能，以守法為懦弱。

translations.literal: Thereupon above and below drove one another, successively applying beating and cudgeling; taking cruelty and violence as capability, taking upholding the law as cowardice.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter superiors and subordinates drove one another to beatings; cruelty counted as capability, upholding the law as cowardice.

sentences.zh: 是時帝意每尚慘急，而姦回不止，京市白日，公行掣盜，人間強盜，亦往往而有。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor's intent always favored cruel urgency, yet treachery did not cease; in the capital in broad daylight, robbers openly snatched; among the people, strong-arm robbers also often existed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor favored cruel urgency, yet crime persisted; robbers snatched goods in broad daylight in the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝患之，問羣臣斷禁之法。

translations.literal: The emperor was troubled by this and asked ministers about methods to stop and prohibit.
translations.idiomatic: Troubled, he asked ministers how to stop it.

sentences.zh: 楊素等未及言，帝曰：「朕知之矣。

translations.literal: Yang Su and others had not yet spoken when the emperor said: "I know it."
translations.idiomatic: Before Yang Su and others could speak, the emperor said: "I know what to do."

sentences.zh: 」詔有能糾告者，沒賊家產業，以賞糾人。

translations.literal: He ordered that those able to impeach and report would confiscate the robber's household property and reward the reporter.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered that informants receive the robber's confiscated property as reward.

sentences.zh: 時月之間，內外寧息。

translations.literal: Within that month, inside and outside were peaceful and quiet.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month, peace was restored.

sentences.zh: 其後無賴之徒，候富人子弟出路者，而故遺物於其前，偶拾取則擒以送官，而取其賞。

translations.literal: After this, worthless fellows waited for wealthy men's sons to go out on the road, deliberately leaving objects before them; if they picked them up by chance, they seized and sent them to officials, taking the reward.
translations.idiomatic: Rogues then laid objects before wealthy youths; if picked up, they seized them and claimed the reward.

sentences.zh: 大抵被陷者甚眾。

translations.literal: Generally those framed were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Many were falsely framed.

sentences.zh: 帝知之，乃命盜一錢已上皆棄市。

translations.literal: The emperor knew this and ordered that stealing one coin and above all were executed in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Learning this, he ordered execution in the market for stealing one coin or more.

sentences.zh: 行旅皆晏起早宿，[14]天下懍懍焉。

translations.literal: Travelers all rested early and departed late, [14] the realm trembled with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Travelers rested early and departed late; [14] the realm trembled with fear.

sentences.zh: 此後又定制，行署取一錢已上，聞見不告言者，坐至死。

translations.literal: After this another regulation was made: for traveling offices taking one coin and above, those who saw and heard but did not report were punished up to death.
translations.idiomatic: Another regulation followed: taking one coin from a traveling office, or failing to report it, was punishable by death.

sentences.zh: 自此四人共盜一榱桶，三人同竊一瓜，事發即時行決。

translations.literal: From this four people jointly stealing one rafter bucket, three people jointly stealing one melon—when the matter was discovered, immediate execution.
translations.idiomatic: Four people stealing one rafter bucket, three stealing one melon—all were immediately executed.

sentences.zh: 有數人劫執事而謂之曰：「吾豈求財者邪？

translations.literal: Several people seized an official and said to him: "Are we not seekers of wealth?
translations.idiomatic: Several men seized an official and said: "Are we seekers of wealth?

sentences.zh: 但為枉人來耳。

translations.literal: We came only for the sake of the wronged.
translations.idiomatic: We came only on behalf of the wronged.

sentences.zh: 而為我奏至尊，自古以來，體國立法，未有盜一錢而死也。

translations.literal: Yet report for us to the Supreme One—since ancient times, establishing the state and making law, never was there death for stealing one coin.
translations.idiomatic: Report to the Supreme One—for since antiquity, no state ever executed a man for stealing one coin.

sentences.zh: 而不為我以聞，吾更來，而屬無類矣。

translations.literal: If you do not report for us, we will come again, and then there will be no more of your kind.
translations.idiomatic: If you do not report for us, we will return, and then there will be none of your kind left.

sentences.zh: 」帝聞之，為停盜取一錢棄市之法。

translations.literal: The emperor heard this and stopped the law of executing in the market for stealing one coin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard this and abolished execution for stealing one coin.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗發怒，六月棒殺人。

translations.literal: The emperor once grew angry and in the sixth month beat people to death.
translations.idiomatic: Once enraged, he beat people to death in the sixth month.

sentences.zh: 大理少卿趙綽固爭曰：「季夏之月，天地成長庶類。

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Court of Justice Zhao Chuo firmly contended saying: "In the fourth month of summer, Heaven and Earth grow and complete the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director Zhao Chuo contended: "In the fourth month of summer, Heaven and Earth nurture all living things.

sentences.zh: 不可以此時誅殺。

translations.literal: One cannot at this time execute and kill.
translations.idiomatic: Execution is forbidden at this season."

sentences.zh: 」帝報曰：「六月雖曰生長，此時必有雷霆。

translations.literal: The emperor replied saying: "The sixth month though called growing, at this time there must be thunder.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "Though the sixth month is a season of growth, thunder must still strike.

sentences.zh: 天道既於炎陽之時，震其威怒，我則天而行，有何不可。

translations.literal: Heaven's Way, since in the season of blazing yang, displays its wrathful thunder, I then act as Heaven and proceed—what is not permitted?
translations.idiomatic: Since Heaven displays wrathful thunder in blazing heat, I act as Heaven—what is forbidden?

sentences.zh: 」遂殺之。

translations.literal: He then killed them.
translations.idiomatic: He executed them anyway.

sentences.zh: 大理掌固來曠上封事，言大理官司恩寬。

translations.literal: Court of Justice clerk Lai Kuang submitted a sealed memorial saying the Court of Justice official Si En was lenient.
translations.idiomatic: Court clerk Lai Kuang submitted a sealed memorial praising Court official Si En for leniency.

sentences.zh: 帝以曠為忠直，遣每旦於五品行中參見。

translations.literal: The emperor thought Kuang was loyal and upright and ordered him each morning to attend among fifth-rank officials.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deemed Kuang loyal and ordered him to attend each morning among fifth-rank officials.

sentences.zh: 曠又告少卿趙綽濫免徒囚，帝使信臣推驗，初無阿曲。

translations.literal: Kuang again reported that Vice Director Zhao Chuo improperly remitted convict laborers; the emperor sent trusted ministers to investigate; initially there was no favoritism.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang then reported that Zhao Chuo improperly released convict laborers; investigation found no favoritism.

sentences.zh: 帝又怒曠，命斬之。

translations.literal: The emperor again was angry at Kuang and ordered execution.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grew angry at Kuang and ordered execution.

sentences.zh: 綽因固爭，以為曠不合死。

translations.literal: Chuo therefore firmly contended, thinking Kuang did not merit death.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo firmly contended that Kuang did not merit death.

sentences.zh: 帝乃拂衣入閣，綽又矯言，臣更不理曠，自有他事未及奏聞。

translations.literal: The emperor then brushed his robes and entered the side chamber; Chuo again falsely said: "Your servant will no longer settle Kuang; there is another matter not yet memorialized."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor brushed his robes and entered the side chamber; Chuo falsely said: "I will no longer settle Kuang; another matter awaits memorial."

sentences.zh: 帝命引入閤，綽再拜請曰：「臣有死罪三。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered him brought into the side chamber; Chuo again bowed and requested saying: "Your servant has three capital crimes.
translations.idiomatic: Brought into the side chamber, Chuo bowed: "I have three capital crimes.

sentences.zh: 臣為大理少卿，不能制馭掌固，使曠觸挂天刑，死罪一也。

translations.literal: Your servant as Vice Director of the Court of Justice could not control and restrain the clerk, causing Kuang to touch and offend Heaven's punishment—capital crime one.
translations.idiomatic: As Vice Director I could not control my clerk, causing Kuang to offend imperial punishment—capital crime one.

sentences.zh: 囚不合死，而臣不能死爭，死罪二也。

translations.literal: The prisoner did not merit death, yet your servant could not contend to the death—capital crime two.
translations.idiomatic: The prisoner did not merit death, yet I could not argue to the death—capital crime two.

sentences.zh: 臣本無他事，而妄言求入，死罪三也。

translations.literal: Your servant originally had no other matter, yet falsely said requesting entry—capital crime three.
translations.idiomatic: I had no other business, yet falsely requested entry—capital crime three."

sentences.zh: 」帝解顏。

translations.literal: The emperor relaxed his expression.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's expression softened.

sentences.zh: 會獻皇后在坐，帝賜綽二金盃酒，飲訖，并以盃賜之。

translations.literal: When Empress Xian was seated, the emperor gave Chuo two golden cups of wine; when finished drinking, both cups were also bestowed on him.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Xian being present, the emperor gave Chuo two golden cups of wine and bestowed the cups on him.

sentences.zh: 曠因免死，配徒廣州。

translations.literal: Kuang thereby escaped death, assigned as convict labor to Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang escaped death and was assigned convict labor in Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 帝以年齡晚暮，尤崇尚佛道，又素信鬼神。

translations.literal: The emperor, as his years grew late, especially honored and esteemed Buddhism and the Way, and also always believed in ghosts and spirits.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years the emperor especially honored Buddhism and believed in ghosts and spirits.

sentences.zh: 二十年，詔沙門道士壞佛像天尊，百姓壞岳瀆神像，皆以惡逆論。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year, an edict said that monks and Daoist priests who destroyed Buddha images or the Heavenly Lord, and common people who destroyed mountain and river spirit images—all were judged as wicked treason.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year, destroying Buddha images, the Heavenly Lord, or mountain and river spirit images was judged wicked treason.

sentences.zh: 帝猜忌，二朝臣僚，用法尤峻。

translations.literal: The emperor was suspicious; toward court officials of the two dynasties, the law was especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: Suspicious toward officials of the two dynasties, he applied the law with especial severity.

sentences.zh: 御史監師，於元正日不劾武官衣劍之不齊者，或以白帝，帝謂之曰：「爾為御史，何縱捨自由。

translations.literal: The censor supervising instructors, on New Year's Day not impeaching military officials for uneven dress and swords, some reported to the emperor; the emperor said to him: "You are a censor—how do you indulge and release freely?"
translations.idiomatic: A censor who failed to impeach military officials for uneven dress on New Year's Day was told: "You are a censor—how do you indulge them?"

sentences.zh: 」命殺之。

translations.literal: Ordered execution.
translations.idiomatic: He was executed.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫毛思祖諫，又殺之。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Grandee Mao Sizu remonstrated; again executed.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Grandee Mao Sizu remonstrated; he too was executed.

sentences.zh: 左領軍府長史考校不平，將作寺丞以諫麥𪌭遲晚，武庫令以署庭荒蕪，獨孤師以受蕃客鸚鵡，帝察知，並親臨斬決。

translations.literal: Left Guard Office chief administrator's examination and judgment was unfair; Construction Office vice director remonstrated that wheat was late; Armory director because the courtyard was overgrown with weeds; Dugu Shi because he received a parrot from foreign guests—the emperor detected and knew, all personally went to execute.
translations.idiomatic: A chief administrator judged unfairly; a vice director remonstrated about late wheat; an armory director's courtyard was overgrown; Dugu Shi received a foreign parrot—the emperor personally executed them all.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，用法益峻，帝既喜怒不恒，不復依準科律。

translations.literal: In the Renshou era, the law grew ever more severe; the emperor's likes and dislikes were not constant; he no longer followed the code as standard.
translations.idiomatic: In the Renshou era the law grew harsher; the emperor's whims replaced the code.

sentences.zh: 時楊素正被委任。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Su was being entrusted with power.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su then held delegated power.

sentences.zh: 素又禀性高下，公卿股慄，不敢措言。

translations.literal: Su also by nature was high and low; dukes and ministers trembled in their legs and did not dare speak.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su's temperament was volatile; officials trembled and dared not speak.

sentences.zh: 素於鴻臚少卿陳延不平，經蕃客館，庭中有馬屎，又庶僕氊上樗蒲。

translations.literal: Su was displeased with Vice Director of the Court of Ceremonies Chen Yan; passing the foreign guests' hostel, in the courtyard there was horse dung, and servants gambling with mulberry seeds on felt.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su disliked Chen Yan; passing the foreign guests' hostel he found horse dung in the courtyard and servants gambling on felt.

sentences.zh: 旋以白帝，帝大怒曰：「主客令不灑掃庭內，掌固以私戲污敗官氊，罪狀何以加此。

translations.literal: Immediately reported to the emperor; the emperor greatly angry said: "The host-guest director did not sweep the courtyard; the clerk privately played and defiled official felt—how can guilt be added to this?"
translations.idiomatic: He reported to the emperor, who raged: "The host-guest director failed to sweep the courtyard; clerks gambled on official felt—how can this be punished enough?"

sentences.zh: 」皆於西市棒殺，而榜棰陳延，殆至於斃。

translations.literal: All were beaten to death at the Western Market, and Chen Yan was posted and cudgeled, nearly to death.
translations.idiomatic: All were beaten to death at the Western Market; Chen Yan was posted and cudgeled nearly to death.

sentences.zh: 大理寺丞楊遠、劉子通等，性愛深文，每隨牙奏獄，能承順帝旨。

translations.literal: Court of Justice vice directors Yang Yuan and Liu Zitong and others by nature loved deep text; each followed the emperor's pleasure in memorializing cases, able to comply with the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Vice directors Yang Yuan and Liu Zitong loved harsh legal prose and tailored cases to the emperor's pleasure.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，並遣於殿庭三品行中供奉，每有詔獄，專使主之。

translations.literal: The emperor greatly pleased, all sent to attend among third-rank officials in the palace hall; whenever there were edict cases, specially dispatched to take charge.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and assigned them to attend among third-rank officials; edict cases were specially entrusted to them.

sentences.zh: 候帝所不快，則案以重抵，無殊罪而死者，不可勝原。

translations.literal: Waiting for what displeased the emperor, then judged with heavy penalty; those dying without special guilt were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was displeased, they applied heavy penalties; countless died without special guilt.

sentences.zh: 遠又能附楊素，每於塗中接候，而以囚名白之，皆隨素所為輕重。

translations.literal: Yuan also could attach to Yang Su; each on the road waited and met, reporting prisoner names to him—all followed Su's light and heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan also attached to Yang Su, reporting prisoner names on the road—all sentences followed Su's whim.

sentences.zh: 其臨終赴市者，莫不塗中呼枉，仰天而哭。

translations.literal: Those at the end going to the market, none did not on the road cry out injustice, looking to Heaven and weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Condemned prisoners cried out injustice on the road to execution, weeping to Heaven.

sentences.zh: 越公素侮弄朝權，帝亦不之能悉。

translations.literal: Duke Yue Su insulted and manipulated court power; the emperor also could not fully know.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Yang Su manipulated court power; the emperor could not fully restrain him.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，以高祖禁網深刻，又敕修律令，除十惡之條。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, because Gaozu's net of prohibition was deep and刻, he again ordered revision of statutes and ordinances, abolishing the ten abominations.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, finding Emperor Wen's prohibitions too harsh, he ordered revision of the code and abolished the ten abominations.

sentences.zh: 時斗稱皆小舊二倍，[15]其贖銅亦加二倍為差。

translations.literal: At that time the dou and scale were all two times smaller than the old, [15] the ransom copper also added two times as the difference.
translations.idiomatic: Measures were half the old size, [15] and redemption copper doubled accordingly.

sentences.zh: 杖百則三十斤矣。

translations.literal: One hundred cudgel strokes then thirty jin.
translations.idiomatic: One hundred cudgel strokes then required thirty jin.

sentences.zh: 徒一年者六十斤，每等加三十斤為差，三年則一百八十斤矣。

translations.literal: One year convict labor sixty jin; each degree added thirty jin as difference; three years then one hundred eighty jin.
translations.idiomatic: One year of convict labor sixty jin; each degree added thirty jin; three years one hundred eighty jin.

sentences.zh: 流無異等，贖二百四十斤。

translations.literal: Exile had no different degrees; ransom two hundred forty jin.
translations.idiomatic: Exile had no gradations; redemption required two hundred forty jin.

sentences.zh: 二死同贖三百六十斤。

translations.literal: Both capital punishments alike ransom three hundred sixty jin.
translations.idiomatic: Both capital forms required three hundred sixty jin for redemption.

sentences.zh: 其實不異。

translations.literal: In substance no difference.
translations.idiomatic: In substance there was no difference.

sentences.zh: 開皇舊制，釁門子弟，不得居宿衞近侍之官。

translations.literal: Kaihuang old system: sons and younger brothers of tainted households could not occupy palace guard and close-attendant offices.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Kaihuang code, sons of tainted households could not hold palace guard or close-attendant posts.

sentences.zh: 先是蕭巖以叛誅，崔君綽坐連庶人勇事，家口籍沒。

translations.literal: Previously Xiao Yan was executed for rebellion; Cui Junzhuo sat connected to the commoner Yong affair; household members' registers confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: Previously Xiao Yan was executed for rebellion; Cui Junzhuo was implicated in Prince Yong's affair; their households were confiscated.

sentences.zh: 巖以中宮故，君綽緣女入宮愛幸，帝乃下詔革前制曰：「罪不及嗣，既弘至孝之道，恩由義斷，以勸事君之節。

translations.literal: Yan because of the empress's connection, Junzhuo because his daughter entered the palace and gained favor—the emperor then issued an edict abolishing the former system saying: "Punishment does not reach descendants—already extending the Way of supreme filial piety; grace cut off by righteousness—to encourage the integrity of serving the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Yan through the empress, Junzhuo through a favored daughter—the emperor abolished the old rule: "Punishment does not reach descendants—extending supreme filial piety; grace severed by righteousness encourages loyalty.

sentences.zh: 故羊鮒從戮，彌見叔向之誠，季布立勳，無預丁公之禍，用能樹聲往代，貽範將來。

translations.literal: Therefore Yang Fuzhi followed execution, further showing Shu Xiang's sincerity; Ji Bu established merit, without involvement in Lord Ding's calamity—thereby able to establish reputation in former generations, leaving a model for the future.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Yang Fuzhi's execution showed Shu Xiang's sincerity; Ji Bu's merit spared Lord Ding's punishment—establishing reputations for posterity.

sentences.zh: 朕虛己為政，思遵舊典，推心待物，每從寬政。

translations.literal: We, emptying ourselves in government, think to follow old canons, treating people with open hearts, each time following lenient government.
translations.idiomatic: We govern with open hearts, following old canons and lenient policy.

sentences.zh: 六位成象，美厥含弘，一眚掩德，甚非謂也。

translations.literal: The six positions forming the image, beautifying that inclusive magnanimity; one fault covering virtue—greatly not what is said.
translations.idiomatic: The six offices embody inclusive magnanimity; one fault should not cover all virtue.

sentences.zh: 諸犯罪被戮之門，期已下親，仍令合仕，聽預宿衞近侍之官。」

translations.literal: All gates of those executed for crimes—relatives below one generation—are still ordered to hold office jointly, permitted to participate in palace guard and close-attendant offices."
translations.idiomatic: Relatives within one generation of executed criminals may again hold office and serve in palace guard and close-attendant posts."

sentences.zh: 三年，新律成。

translations.literal: In the third year, the new code was completed.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the new code was completed.

sentences.zh: 凡五百條，為十八篇。

translations.literal: Five hundred articles in all, eighteen chapters.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred articles in eighteen chapters.

sentences.zh: 詔施行之，謂之大業律：一曰名例，二曰衞宮，三曰違制，四曰請求，五曰戶，六曰婚，七曰擅興，八曰告劾，九曰賊，十曰盜，十一曰鬬，十二曰捕亡，十三曰倉庫，十四曰廐牧，十五曰關市，十六曰雜，十七曰詐偽，十八曰斷獄。

translations.literal: An edict ordered its implementation, called the Daye Code: first, Names and Examples; second, Palace Guard; third, Violating Regulations; fourth, Requests; fifth, Households; sixth, Marriage; seventh, Unauthorized Mobilization; eighth, Accusation and Impeachment; ninth, Bandits; tenth, Robbers; eleventh, Fighting; twelfth, Pursuit of Fugitives; thirteenth, Granaries and Storehouses; fourteenth, Stables and Herds; fifteenth, Passes and Markets; sixteenth, Miscellaneous; seventeenth, Fraud and Forgery; eighteenth, Trial and Judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Promulgated as the Daye Code in eighteen chapters: Names and Examples, Palace Guard, Violating Regulations, Requests, Households, Marriage, Unauthorized Mobilization, Accusation and Impeachment, Bandits, Robbers, Fighting, Pursuit of Fugitives, Granaries and Storehouses, Stables and Herds, Passes and Markets, Miscellaneous, Fraud and Forgery, and Trial and Judgment.

sentences.zh: 其五刑之內，降從輕典者，二百餘條。

translations.literal: Within the five punishments, those reduced and following the lighter canon were over two hundred articles.
translations.idiomatic: Over two hundred articles within the five punishments were reduced toward leniency.

sentences.zh: 其枷杖決罰訊囚之制，並輕於舊。

translations.literal: Its cangue, cudgel, deciding punishment, and interrogating prisoners—all lighter than the old.
translations.idiomatic: Cangue, cudgel, sentencing, and interrogation were all lighter than before.

sentences.zh: 是時百姓久厭嚴刻，喜於刑寬。

translations.literal: At that time the common people long weary of strictness and刻, rejoiced at the leniency of punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The people, long weary of harshness, rejoiced at leniency.

sentences.zh: 後帝乃外征四夷，內窮嗜慾，兵革歲動，賦斂滋繁。

translations.literal: Afterward the emperor then externally campaigned against the four barbarians, internally exhausted by desires; war and weapons moved yearly, levies and exactions grew ever more numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he campaigned against foreign powers and indulged his desires; war and levies grew ever heavier.

sentences.zh: 有司皆臨時迫脅，苟求濟事，憲章遐棄，賄賂公行，窮人無告，聚為盜賊。

translations.literal: Relevant offices all temporarily coerced, hastily seeking to accomplish matters; statutes and regulations were abandoned afar; bribes walked openly; the poor had nowhere to report; they gathered as bandits and robbers.
translations.idiomatic: Officials coerced and extorted; statutes were abandoned; bribery flourished; the poor turned to banditry.

sentences.zh: 帝乃更立嚴刑，勑天下竊盜已上，罪無輕重，不待聞奏，皆斬。

translations.literal: The emperor then again established severe punishment, ordering that throughout the realm for robbery and above, guilt regardless of light or heavy, without awaiting memorial and report, all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: He then imposed severe punishment: all robbery and above, regardless of severity, was beheaded without awaiting imperial review.

sentences.zh: 百姓轉相羣聚，攻剽城邑，誅罰不能禁。

translations.literal: The common people in turn gathered in groups, attacking and plundering cities and towns; punishment and execution could not prohibit.
translations.idiomatic: People gathered in bands, attacking towns; punishment could not stop them.

sentences.zh: 帝以盜賊不息，乃益肆淫刑。

translations.literal: The emperor because bandits and robbers did not cease, then further indulged in excessive punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Because banditry did not cease, he further indulged excessive punishment.

sentences.zh: 九年，又詔為盜者籍沒其家。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, another edict said that robbers' household registers were confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, robbers' household registers were confiscated.

sentences.zh: 自是羣賊大起，郡縣官人，又各專威褔，生殺任情矣。

translations.literal: From this great bands of robbers arose; prefectural and county officials again each monopolized authority and blessing, life and death at their feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Great bands of robbers arose; prefectural officials again held life-and-death power at whim.

sentences.zh: 及楊玄感反，帝誅之，罪及九族。

translations.literal: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, the emperor executed him; guilt reached the nine clans.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, the emperor executed him and punished nine generations of his clan.

sentences.zh: 其尤重者，行轘裂梟首之刑。

translations.literal: For the most severe, dismemberment at the waist and exposing the head were applied.
translations.idiomatic: The most severe cases received dismemberment and exposure of the head.

sentences.zh: 或磔而射之，命公卿已下，臠噉其肉。

translations.literal: Some were dismembered and shot; ordered from dukes and ministers downward to carve and devour the flesh.
translations.idiomatic: Some were dismembered and shot; dukes and ministers downward were ordered to carve and devour the flesh.

sentences.zh: 百姓怨嗟，天下大潰，及恭帝即位，獄訟有歸焉。

translations.literal: The common people groaned in resentment; the realm greatly collapsed; when Emperor Gong ascended the throne, lawsuits and litigation had a place to go.
translations.idiomatic: The people groaned in resentment; the realm collapsed; when Emperor Gong took the throne, justice again had a place.

sentences.zh: 校勘記

translations.literal: Collation Notes
translations.idiomatic: Collation Notes

sentences.zh: 實難去弊 冊府六一０，「弊」作「取」。

translations.literal: Shi nan qu bi — Cefu yuangui 610 has "qu" as "取" (take).
translations.idiomatic: For "shi nan qu bi," Cefu yuangui 610 reads "qu" as "取" (take).

sentences.zh: 斗械 「斗」原作「升」，據冊府六一０改。

translations.literal: Dou xie — "Dou" originally read "升" (sheng); corrected according to Cefu yuangui 610.
translations.idiomatic: "Dou xie": "Dou" originally read "sheng"; corrected per Cefu yuangui 610.

sentences.zh: 下文「斗械」，據冊府二六一改。

translations.literal: Below, "dou xie," corrected according to Cefu yuangui 261.
translations.idiomatic: The following "dou xie" is corrected per Cefu yuangui 261.

sentences.zh: 熟靼不去廉 「靼」原作「靻」。

translations.literal: Shu ta bu qu lian — "Ta" originally read "靻" (zu).
translations.idiomatic: "Shu ta bu qu lian": "Ta" originally read "zu."

sentences.zh: 御覽六四九引晉令也作「靻」，御覽注：「柔革也。

translations.literal: Imperial Readings 649 citing Jin ordinances also has "靻," with a note: "Soft hide."
translations.idiomatic: Imperial Readings 649, citing Jin ordinances, also has "zu," glossed as "soft hide."

sentences.zh: 」按：說文解字「靼，柔革也」；

translations.literal: According to Shuowen jiezi: "Ta, soft hide also."
translations.idiomatic: Shuowen jiezi reads: "Ta, soft hide."

sentences.zh: 「靻」始見于廣韻。

translations.literal: "Zu" first appears in Guangyun.
translations.idiomatic: "Zu" first appears in Guangyun.

sentences.zh: 是此字應作「靼」，不作「靻」，今改正。

translations.literal: This character should read "ta," not "zu"; now corrected.
translations.idiomatic: The character should read "ta," not "zu"; corrected here.

sentences.zh: 下同。

translations.literal: The same below.
translations.idiomatic: The same correction applies below.

sentences.zh: 廣三分 「分」原作「寸」，據御覽六四九改。

translations.literal: Guang san fen — "Fen" originally read "cun" (inch); corrected according to Imperial Readings 649.
translations.idiomatic: "Guang san fen": "Fen" originally read "cun"; corrected per Imperial Readings 649.

sentences.zh: 其以職員應罰 「員」疑當作「負」。

translations.literal: Qi yi zhi yuan ying fa — "Yuan" is suspected to should read "fu" (demerit).
translations.idiomatic: "Qi yi zhi yuan ying fa": "Yuan" is suspected to read "fu" (demerit).

sentences.zh: 下文，北齊「鞭杖十為一負」，隋「贖銅一斤為一負」。

translations.literal: Below, Northern Qi has "ten whip or cudgel strokes equal one demerit"; Sui has "one jin of ransom copper equals one demerit."
translations.idiomatic: Below, Northern Qi has "ten whip or cudgel strokes equal one demerit"; Sui has "one jin of ransom copper equals one demerit."

sentences.zh: 於事為劇 「事」原作「辛」，據冊府二六一改。

translations.literal: Yu shi wei ju — "Shi" originally read "xin" (辛); corrected according to Cefu yuangui 261.
translations.idiomatic: "Yu shi wei ju": "Shi" originally read "xin"; corrected per Cefu yuangui 261.

sentences.zh: 鎖二重 冊府六一一，「鎖」作「鉗」。

translations.literal: Suo er chong — Cefu yuangui 611 has "suo" as "qian" (cangue).
translations.idiomatic: "Suo er chong": Cefu yuangui 611 reads "suo" as "qian" (cangue).

sentences.zh: 下「並鎖一重」同。

translations.literal: Below "bing suo yi chong" the same.
translations.idiomatic: The same applies to "bing suo yi chong" below.

sentences.zh: 不計階品 冊府六一一，「不計」作「亦許」。

translations.literal: Bu ji jie pin — Cefu yuangui 611 has "bu ji" as "yi xu" (also permitted).
translations.idiomatic: "Bu ji jie pin": Cefu yuangui 611 reads "bu ji" as "yi xu" (also permitted).

sentences.zh: 不加宮刑 「宮」原作「害」，據冊府六一一改。

translations.literal: Bu jia gong xing — "Gong" originally read "hai" (harm); corrected according to Cefu yuangui 611.
translations.idiomatic: "Bu jia gong xing": "Gong" originally read "hai"; corrected per Cefu yuangui 611.

sentences.zh: 正長隱五戶及十丁以上及地三頃以上 「丁」上原脫「十」字，「頃」上原脫「三」字，據周書武帝紀下補。

translations.literal: Zheng zhang yin wu hu ji shi ding yi shang ji di san qing yi shang — "Shi" above originally lacked "ten"; above "qing" originally lacked "three"; supplemented according to Zhou shu, Wudi ji xia.
translations.idiomatic: For the passage on village heads concealing five households, ten adult males, and three qing of land: "ten" above "ding" and "three" above "qing" were missing; supplemented per Zhou shu, Wudi ji xia.

sentences.zh: 通鑑一七三，「三頃」作「頃」。

translations.literal: Zizhi tongjian 173 has "san qing" as "qing" ( acre).
translations.idiomatic: Zizhi tongjian 173 reads "san qing" as "qing" (acre).

sentences.zh: 其流徒之罪皆減從輕 「流」原作「法」，據冊府六一一改。

translations.literal: Qi liu tu zhi zui jie jian cong qing — "Liu" originally read "fa" (law); corrected according to Cefu yuangui 611.
translations.idiomatic: "Qi liu tu zhi zui jie jian cong qing": "Liu" originally read "fa"; corrected per Cefu yuangui 611.

sentences.zh: 三流同比徒三年 「同」原作「周」，據通典一六四、冊府六一一、唐律疏義名例改。

translations.literal: San liu tong bi tu san nian — "Tong" originally read "zhou" (周); corrected according to Tongdian 164, Cefu yuangui 611, and Tang lü shuyi, mingli.
translations.idiomatic: "San liu tong bi tu san nian": "Tong" originally read "zhou"; corrected per Tongdian 164, Cefu yuangui 611, and Tang lü shuyi.

sentences.zh: 至省仍不理 原脫「至」字，據通典一六四、冊府六一一補。

translations.literal: Zhi sheng reng bu li — "Zhi" was originally missing; supplemented according to Tongdian 164 and Cefu yuangui 611.
translations.idiomatic: "Zhi sheng reng bu li": "Zhi" was originally missing; supplemented per Tongdian 164 and Cefu yuangui 611.

sentences.zh: 晏起早宿 「早」原作「晚」，據御覽六四六改。

translations.literal: Yan qi zao su — "Zao" originally read "wan" (late); corrected according to Imperial Readings 646.
translations.idiomatic: "Yan qi zao su": "Zao" originally read "wan" (late); corrected per Imperial Readings 646.

sentences.zh: 斗稱 「斗」原作「升」，據冊府六一一改。

translations.literal: Dou cheng — "Dou" originally read "sheng" (升); corrected according to Cefu yuangui 611.
translations.idiomatic: "Dou cheng": "Dou" originally read "sheng"; corrected per Cefu yuangui 611.
